reviews.text: Visited to try the new Christmas cocktails in the seasonal yurt and loved every minute! The firepits and fairy lights make the yurt so warm and cosy, perfect for a casual Christmassy date night. The biscotti sour and snowjito were our favourites. @nottinghillfoodie_

Went for a drag show, really liked the place. Would love to go back to check the roof top and the upper floor just for a drink.
To be honest, my favourite thing about the place was the ladies loo- probably the coolest WC in London. 👑

It's like a TARDIS when you walk inside and the rooftop bar is truly stunning. The basement club is a decent enough size if you like a genuinely intimate but not claustrophobic experience with basic seating near the stage and adequate sound system and lighting. Staff seem cheerful and friendly.

Really not happy with my experience. I was out for a friends birthday and asked the supposed “manager” to put my phone on charge in which she said yes. After about 10 minutes i asked for my phone back then she proceeded to tell me i never gave it to her, it was only when i told the other members of staff they got my phone back straight away after i told the manager i will write a bad review on her and she panicked . Wish i could remember the names of the staff who helped me as they was lovely and im very greatful for them helping me!
Please be careful of the “manager”

2nd time here and each time it’s more disappointing. Awful music, no atmosphere, rude staff.
Came for a comedy evening and Eventbrite had only issued 1 barcode for our tickets (a simple error I’m sure) but despite showing all of the confirmation emails they said we needed to buy another ticket at double the online price. Would not listen to reason or take into account the paper trail.
I’d advise you to swerve Queen of Hoxton and go to any of the other great venues close by.

Great experience! The dining section upstairs is a nice relief from downstairs. The food was incredible- the marmite butter was 10/10. Pie was also lovely. I will say service could’ve been better, our waiter was unsure and awkward but perhaps he was just learning!

🍺 £6.70 Princess Pilsner

The Princess of Shoreditch sits in a quiet backstreet in Shoreditch, East London, the nearest Tube is Old Street.

Records show there’s been a pub on this site since 1742. It was rebuilt in the 19th century and started life as a Whitbread house named The Princess Royal.

This is a one-bar, two-room gastropub with an elegant understated, “less is more” feel. The bright and airy ground-floor bar features a traditional servery and an impressive bar back. There’s plenty of seating with low tables, chairs, and leather banquettes. Decorative touches include a huge mirror and a lovely old Whitbread sign above the door.

Upstairs, reached via a wrought-iron spiral staircase, is the dining room. It’s stylish with a boarded floor, fireplace, green walls, black-and-white prints of the local area, and neatly set tables and chairs.

The beer selection offers a small but varied keg lineup. Three cask pumps were present but not on when I visited. I opted for the Princess Pilsner — excellent pint, though at a slightly above-average price. The food menu is seasonal British fare, focused on local sourced ingredients. Fish and chips is £21, and I hear the sticky toffee pudding is a must.

I arrived just after 12:30pm on a mild Saturday lunchtime in October. The pub had just opened, and I was the only punter in. The atmosphere was relaxed, with a calming soundtrack setting the tone. Service was spot on — the two staff on duty were friendly, busy preparing for the day, and happy to show me around.

Sometimes the word “gastro” puts off those just after a pint, but this pub balances both worlds nicely — a bar for casual drinking and a smart space for a proper meal.

I really enjoyed my visit. The Whitbread heritage, the striking architecture, the understated decor, the spiral staircase, and a perfectly poured pint all made for a great stop.

Follow @princessofshoreditch for updates.

Our first time trying a Sunday roast and it didn't disappoint! We had a beef roast which was as delicious as the reviews say. Our dining experience was made even greater because our server Christina was so warm and welcoming. She put us right at ease. Thank you so much for the amazing experience. Will definitely come again.

This was a huge disappointment given the price of the Christmas set menu. My venison main turned up not just cold but refrigerated and very dry, had to send it back. The sticky toffee pudding was clearly from a packet, dry, looked like a stale muffin. The rest of our team thought their chicken main was completely average. There were no pigs in blankets even though the menu said there would be. Staff were friendly but drinks service was comically slow. We managed to get two drinks each in the space of over two hours. At £60 per head for the set menu it was really very poor. Christmas party ruined!

Visited for a Friday night dinner with 2 friends and wow, were we impressed with the food!
We were recommended a few dishes by our waitress and the chef, which didn’t disappoint. Absolute must haves are the scotch egg (the best we have ever had), marmite glazed chicken thigh, scallops with black pudding butter, and duck breast. Leave room for dessert as they were delightful!
Service was well paced and we were well looked after. A lovely ambience with great interiors- more of a restaurant vibe than a pub. A great place for date night or for dinner with friends. Will be back soon to try the rest of the menu!

I love All Star Lanes! I was excited to visit this branch when visiting the area, I would go all the time if I lived nearer. They always have a cool retro vibe and I enjoy the more boutique setting, it makes a change from large loud bowling alleys. Plus you can stop for a bite to eat in their restaurant area or enjoy a cocktail in their swanky bar space. A perfect place for a date actually. On my visit, the staff were friendly and went out of their way to make my day. Excellent service ✨!

Booked in Karoake. The floors were very sticky which is quite annoying, it would have been good if they kept the floor clean. Lots of options for songs and was fun. Wish it was a bit brighter in the room

PSA: they will contact you and promise a response within 3 days and not answer after 10 days and still counting. This is extremely poor. Not even a phone number to chase this up. Avoid and take your money elsewhere.

Original review as follows.
Went for Karaoke, arrived around 20mins early and was told to come back closer to booking, so we went and got a drink which was decent price and was of good quality. Once in the room, it was not properly cleaned / sanitised as we went in immediately after another group with no time in-between for a reset for example so this was a concern. Once in the room, the song choice was lacking. Halfway through, the TV screen used turned off and we had to waste paid booking time to resolve this and was not offered extra time after a mistake that was out of our control. One of the microphones also stopped working halfway through which was due to the battery dying which again we had to leave through our paid time and was not resolved as it still kept on dying. This overall a mid experience, and I would not recommend or consider visiting again. Please can this feedback be taken onboard and I would like to request compensation for this poor experience.

Terrible shady looking street with some vintage shops, food on the street isn’t tasty except 1-2 restaurants. Worth mentioning a hidden gem - a handmade chocolates and very tasty hot chocolate served in a chocolate shop. Its the only one on the street.

We visited on Sunday around lunchtime, and the place wasn’t busy, making for a really relaxed atmosphere.

They use a string pin system that just worked; we had zero technical issues.

They no longer make you wear the in-house bowling shoes, which means once checked in, you can go straight to the lane.

We paid £25 per person for 2 games, which felt worth it for the quality of the lanes.

Perfect spot if you want a smooth, hassle-free game in Shoreditch

reviews.text:
I’ve been here several times before because it’s one of my friend’s favourite restaurants, and since my brother was visiting, I wanted to bring him along. I had originally booked for 9:00 pm, but after walking for hours we arrived at 8:00 pm, thankfully, they were happy to seat us earlier with no issues.

We were welcomed with papadum served alongside two sauces (one yogurt‑based and the other slightly spicier) plus some vegetables as starters. Tap water was readily available on the table.

We ordered the mutton tikka, which I can’t recommend enough, the flavour and texture were fantastic. For mains, we had the Karahi king prawn and the aloo meat (potato and lamb) curry. Both dishes were delicious and very filling. We also had pilau rice and one of my favourite items on the menu: the Peshwari naan (coconut).

Everything was excellent, the food arrived quickly, and the staff were very friendly. Highly recommended if you’re in Whitechapel.

One of the best proper curry houses in London, with authentic flavours in a busy and popular environment.

Bring your own booze, or don’t have any, there are soft drink options which accompany the meal nicely.

The lamb chops and garlic naan are outstanding, and all the curry dishes are great.

Sometimes a little wait if you don’t have a reservation but it’s easy to see why as it’s always packed, across 3 floors. At lunchtime it can be a bit quieter, eg Sunday afternoon.

Is a great evening out with a group, the atmosphere is energetic and the food arrives quickly after ordering, and doesn’t disappoint.

Fair prices, consistent quality and a fun visit.

A great experience here. The atmosphere is lively, and it was completely packed. I would definitely book in advance - even this doesn’t guarantee you a table, it just pushes you to the front of the queue! The food itself was absolutely delicious - so flavoursome, and so much of it. The meat biryani (the house special on a Friday night) was unreal.
The service was attentive and friendly, and the prices were fair, especially for London. I’d highly recommend this restaurant - thank you very much

Tayyabs never fails to impress. I tried the fish curry this time and it was honestly to die for—perfectly spiced and so fresh. It even comes with a complimentary salad which is a nice touch. Just a heads up: this place is a powerhouse. Even on a Tuesday at 4:00 PM, it was already buzzing and very busy, so plan accordingly. Highly recommend!

One of my all-time favourite places for Punjabi food.

I always go straight for the tandoori lamb chops. They arrive sizzling from the tandoor with deep char, spice, and incredible flavour. I love the dry lamb or mutton curry and the saag paneer alongside it, with a fresh garlic and coriander naan to mop everything up.

The place is always buzzing. I like that you can see the kitchen working flat out and the food still comes quickly despite how busy it is.

It’s only a few minutes walk from Aldgate East tube. There’s no alcohol licence, but they will put a bottle opener on the table and there’s a good selection of chilled beers a few doors down to bring with you.

Big flavours, serious char, and the smell of spice in the air that happily follows me home.

place was pretty cool however extremely loud. had a great time last night being served by Joao being both a great bar tender and small-talk-companion

Julie was a killer host with her fluffy bucket hat sorting out any and all problems that arose during my time at the book club

not sure of the man’s name but whoever was also working in kitchen was great sorting out any mistakes that arose with food, even if they were mine!

would recommend, the staff were all more than just friendly - you feel like you’re talking to a real human and not a customer service bot

security was also very present making sure to make the place both feel and look secure for its customers

in short, 10/10 experience and will recommend to friends

I used this spot to network with a potential vendor and get some work done. I love the vibe of this place. There's plenty of seating that comfortable. It's also a dynamic space too that has a good mix of play and work which I like. The food is hearty and filling at the right price. This is a great place to meet friend and socialize or get some work done. It depends on what time of the day you show up.

The vibe was nice, the venue itself is very pretty and the music was good - they also serve food up to a certain time. However, the entry fee on the day we went was £10 and a double vodka coke was £10.50, so the drinks and entry are quite standard for London. My experience with the bouncers was positive at first (although I've seen others reviewing that they were not so lucky). Later in the evening, my friend wasn't let back in even though his wrist was stamped and our girl friends were let back in - there seems to be some kind of selective entry after a certain time. There were some people in the club who were very clearly there to start a fight - kept intentionally bumping in to people and then getting angry, so the place can attract a bit of a weird crowd. Otherwise, the club in itself was pretty cool!

Very good breakfast (strictly 5!), good menu, nice place & kind service. Also suitable for big groups. The cappuccino was....far from our standard, not tasty, but the gladly gave us a refund with a smile. We find it great attitude & service.

Been here both during the day and evening. Brunch is not bad, but I’ve definitely had better, especially the bread. When I came there were quite a few things not available even though it was the start of Sunday brunch, so was a bit disappointed.

During the evening the place gets really crowded but the music is decent and the downstairs becomes a dance floor. It’s a lot cleaner and nicer than many clubs and bars in the nearby area.

I went there with a group of friends for Sunday roast. We were sat upstairs which was a welcoming and pleasant space.

The roast cam quickly after the order and we were pleasantly surprised. The portions were large and had plenty of vegetables in -the chicken roast to share in particular was a huge portion. The chicken and veggies were very well cooked. My friends said that the beef was quite tough, though.

Service was polite and helpful.

I would definitely return.

Okay guys, we need to talk seriously😆
This potato with ox cheeks is absolutely mind-blowing🤤
If I understood correctly, it’s part of the festive menu.
If you’re booking a Christmas party here you absolutely have to order this dish.
The booking manager and waitress Karyna were incredibly attentive.
The food and drinks were outstanding — thank you!
LOVE THIS PUB I hosted a charity fundraiser pub quiz here. The staff were so lovely, helpful and fun. The space upstairs (the Jago) is great for private events. Thank you so much for having us!

We were there for Christmas Day meal.  It was prefix  so it was what would be a standard Sunday roast meal.  Top 5 worst meals I’ve ever had.  Basically a pile of slop on my plate.  The vegetables were under cooked and the meat was so over covered it was barely edible (let alone cuttable).  Yorkshire pudding tasted like chemicals. It took 3.5 hrs for the complete meal!  There were probably 35 people dining in the pub.  They should stick with pouring beer and leave the cooking to the professionals.

Such a gem! Came here for a casual dinner and was really impressed. The roast beef was perfectly cooked and full of flavour. Loads of beers on tap — something for everyone’s taste. Service was quick and genuinely warm, waiter Karina was amazing . Definitely one of the best pubs in the area.

name: Diwana
address: 96 Brick Ln, Greater, Bethnal Green, London E1 6RL, UK

reviews.text: My girlfriend’s favourite cuisine is the Indian one and she is always on the lookout for some new Indian restaurant, where we have not been and the food is authentic, the ambience cozy and this is how we happened to have found this lovely spot with great lunch specials for about 7 quid!! Impressive deal and even more impressive buffet, where you can really can help yourself with some really tasty dishes! I don’t think that you can beat that! It may get a bit crammed at times, but that is quite understandable, giving the price.

I have no bad impressions regarding the service, quality of food, so as the taste and variety of dishes I have been able to have so far in Diwana. When possible, I am always trying to have my lunch in here and take advantage of the great price and generous portions you get for it! The place is not offering a high-end ambience, but I don’t think that if you are keen for Indian cuisine, such factors would matter, at least they don’t matter for me at all!

This is the best Indian restaurant in this area. The best Indian food that I ever tasted! They offer a great selection of vegetarian dishes. All are surely delicious and good to taste. Perfectly made up of healthy and fresh ingredients. Definitely a perfect spot to all vegetarian and health conscious locals. Very simply but surely feed your appetite.  Service is great as well as the ambiance. The staffs were very friendly and attentive. I loved to go back here again on my next visit.

I've been going to the Diwana since I was a kid. It was excellent 30 odd years ago, and literally nothing has changed. This is an amazing achievement for a restaurant in central London to stay this good and this reasonably priced for so long. I've been going to the Diwana about once per month for all this time, and although quality inevitably does vary (chefs change shifts, you get more or less cardamom in your Lassi), it's still always phenomenal value and usually, one of the best Indian vegetarian meals you can buy in London. The coconut chutney is wonderful, the panni puris are delicious and fun to play with, and the deluxe dosa is a reliable treat. They are also very vegan friendly and will happily make you some non-dairy coconut chutney if you ask. Obviously I'm biased as I've been going here my entire life and feel sentimental about it, but having watched so many family restaurants in London get successful, renovate, expand, then kick up the prices or lower the quality of the food - it's really impressive that this restaurant has been such a reliable and constant part of London life. That's what the fifth star is for!

It was a Sunday afternoon and we were looking to eat lunch before we hopped back on the train at Euston station and we found this place. It ticked all the boxes - cheap but good food. The place was full of customers but they quickly found us a table. The selection of food on offer for the buffet was very good - everything tasted good and seconds were a must! We left with bellies filled, satisfied and would happily come again.

e had an amazing experience at Sushi Samba London. The atmosphere was incredible, the food was outstanding, and the service made the night even more special. Sameera was absolutely fantastic — she was friendly, attentive, and made sure everything was perfect for us throughout the evening. Her warm personality and great recommendations really enhanced our visit. Thank you, Sameera, for making our time at Sushi Samba such a memorable one. We will definitely be back!

I took a friend, my nephew and 2 of my nieces here on a visit to the UK as an opportunity to spend time with them, enjoy some food and a birthday celebration.

The location is really wonderful on the 39th floor (enjoy the glass-walled elevator rides) of a London skyscraper and we were fortunate to be there on a beautiful early Spring evening with clear views across the city.

My guests enjoyed sake, wine and a lychee-elderflower cocktail while we all attacked some edamame. Then we enjoyed the Japanese Eggplant tempura, taquitos (lobster and tuna) before some ngiri, sashimi, steak, black cod and sushi rolls.

Desserts of Japanese crumble, banana-chocolate pie and mochi disappeared quickly.

Service was very good and attentive; a couple of drinks and one dish didn't arrive but were brought promptly when we reminded the waiter. The ambience is good: buzzy, not loud but a good background level. We could all chat and hear one another easily. Fantastic views and an interesting arbor-like frame arches above the tables.

We all really enjoyed ourselves!

Went for valentines lunch and view was nice but definitely better in the evening. We had the special valentines cocktails but we didn’t drink as we didn’t like them! But the Polaroids they did was cute although only one was clear. Staff were super friendly and helpful with gluten free and dairy free choices and black cod was epic, sushi average and samba salad was also divine. For £165 for 2 it was overpriced for us

Good quality food and beautiful view. Only negative you have 2h and have to leave.

We arrived bit late and I felt rushed to eat my food and make sure I try dessert too as it was my first time over there.

The money you pay for the food and service should let you stay longer.

Waitresses didn’t seem very happy, probably overworked and underpaid.

Had our mum's 60th birthday meal here and food was as always good, but the Churrasco Rio Grande was overall better last time we had it here compared to now, maybe it was the seasoning. Samba rolls are amazing though. We ordered desserts and when they arrived, one had a candle with it and given to the birthday celebrant. It wasn't complimentary, it was included in the bill.

We had a truly wonderful evening at Galvin La Chapelle. The food was outstanding from start to finish. Refined, beautifully executed, and clearly driven by an impressive attention to detail. Every course felt thoughtful and intentional, and the overall experience made us feel genuinely special. The elegance of the space only amplifies that feeling. It’s a stunning room and a place that clearly takes pride in excellence.

That said, there were a few moments that slightly broke the magic. We could hear the service director being very harsh with one of the waitstaff several times, right behind our table. We completely understand that a Michelin-starred level of service demands precision and high standards, but those kinds of call-outs would be far better handled discreetly or in private. Hearing it repeatedly made us uncomfortable and genuinely felt bad for the server.

In a bizarrely human and unforgettable twist to the night, we later had two waitstaff members standing behind our table and one of them let out an absolutely legendary fart. It was so unexpected that we couldn’t help but laugh hard. Maybe it was the final personal touch of the evening, certainly memorable and will live forever with us.

All things considered, we had a great night, enjoyed incredible food, first class service and would absolutely recommend the restaurant. We’d happily return and look forward to doing so again soon.

Having been long time fans of the Galvin’s food, we were so pleased when Galvin La Chapelle opened on our doorstep back in 2009.

We dined here on their opening night and have been regular guests since.

It’s been fantastic to enjoy the food here over the years, always precise, technical and tasty. Consistency and standards have remained high.

Service continues to be professional and polite and the dining room is probably my favourite in London.

Today we enjoyed the special Toast and Taste Menu. 5 courses and a drink for only £49. A bargain for Michelin starred cooking in central London.

An easy recommendation for a special lunch in lovey surroundings.

We went to Galvin La Chapelle for the  lunch tasting menu.

It was a beautiful restaurant with a warm and stylish decor. The bare ceiling made it especially interesting and a contrast to the aesthetic of the rest of the restaurant. It looks like it may have been a church.

The staff were very attentive and explained each course. The food itself was very interesting with a mixture of flavours and textures which were delightful. I would love to return to try their a la carte menu.

Overall, a very pleasant lunch.

We were given an amazing gift experience at Galvin La Chapelle for a three-course set menu with a glass of sparkling wine, and it was truly wonderful. We went for my birthday, and it made the day feel so special.

The staff were incredibly welcoming and genuinely kind from the moment we arrived. Every member of the team was exceptional. Dom and Matt were so attentive, the maître d’ was wonderfully warm, and the lady who served us dessert was absolutely lovely.

The whole meal was delightful, and we felt so well looked after throughout.
We’ll definitely be coming back.

I came here for dinner by myself.

Overall, this place has a Bailie, unique and magical ambience. The interior of an old chapel is one of the more unique and charming Settings for a restaurant that I have ever seen.

I will say that my expectations were very high, as a place has Michelin  star. Overall, the Service was very good, but not extraordinary. The food was excellent, but again – I was not as impressed with the food as I would have expected – I feel the food that I got at sketch. Two nights ago was much more, outstanding, and culinary. Perfect and unique.

Overall, I would be unlikely to return at the Price point, but it is a quality restaurant, and I do feel that it is deserving of it status.

A table for two arrived at 5:30 on Thursday and we only waited about 20 minutes.  The restaurant was packed inside but organised.

We ordered the steak rare, which was cooked to a perfect Basc medium rare. The fries were delicious and the sauce was spot on. I also highly recommend the rum cake for dessert.

The service was fantastic and incredibly fast.  The only menu item offered was steak and fries, which explains the quick turnover.

Wait wasn't too bad after 8.30pm on Saturday.
Salad was fresh with a strong mustard dressing. Our waitress forgot to bring our baguette and it was not warm when it was brought to us (without butter). Steak wasn't very hot, and second serving came shortly after first serving arrived.
Profiteroles looked good, but sold out very quickly. Probably best to order at the start of the meal.
Mont blanc was very disappointing, there was limited chestnut purée and full of cream.

This is simple french dining, dont expect it to be extraordinary. It's simple menu of salad for starter, fries as a side and two servings of meat with a nice gravy sauce. Considering the price in the location, I would say this was a decent affordable meal. So I'm happy with the food option. Dessert was also delicious! Service as you come in is lacking, I know the french are not known for customer service, but it is necessary in London? I don't know, but the waitress that actually served our food was really nice (sadly didn't get her name). Highly recommend for a dinner for two, or a small group

Went on a wet Saturday afternoon. Got there around 11.50 and was second line. By 12 maybe  about 6 or 7 couples.
Ordered one rare and 3 medium.
Got the salad which I liked but maybe put too much dressing.
Bread was nice but no butter!!!!!
We all preferred the rare which was my one and unfortunately had to share it with the rest of the family.  I seriously couldn't really taste much of the sauce that it was famous for.  Felt like it needed more flavor.  All those YouTube videos may have exaggerated the taste. This is very subjective.
Chips were great.
Service was ok. No complaints.

When we left at 1pm there was still plenty of tables.

For family of 4 and one bottled water it came to £151.33

Good experience.

Everything was excellent! We arrived at around 6pm on a weekday and were seated almost straight away. The service was very speedy and the food - from the salad and steak to the fries and chocolate cake - was excellent. We’d definitely visit again.

Came for brunch and we were not disappointed. Great menu with lots of choices. Definitely something for everyone.
Food was freshly prepared and beautifully presented.
Juices were amazing!
Staff very friendly and professional.
We had hoped to visit the secret bar but unfortunately it didn’t open till later! Maybe next time!

Had a splendid time at the Breakfast Club on Sunday! I came in with my colleagues as we had our team building event and we had the perfect morning before work!

Eleanor was amazing from the get go, she served us with professionalism and warmth. She was really sweet and provided exceptional customer service to the entire team.

The food was amazing too! I ordered the Full Monty and it was the best full English breakfast I've ever had. It was super filling and I skipped lunch for the day haha!

Thanks to Eleanor and the entire team at Breakfast Club Spitalfields, I'll definitely visit again and get as many people as I can. Highly recommend visiting!

Specifically, The Mayor of Scaredy Cat Town.
Great setup, was a surprise for my partner so she was a bit confused about the Smeg as I'm sure a lot of people are.
Service in TMoSCT was excellent, very attentive, always keeping an eye on your drinks levels.  Food was lovely too!  Really cool atmosphere.
Bottomless Brunch is decent value for money.
Highly recommend.

We had a wonderful time at The Breakfast Club in Spitalfields! My partner is lactose intolerant and they kindly offered plant based pancakes — they were absolutely delicious. We also enjoyed two creamy oat milk cappuccinos, simply perfect.

A very special thank you to Aoife, our lovely waitress💖💖. She was not only sweet and attentive, but also took the time to recommend fun activities for our trip. Her kindness truly made our experience unforgettable🥰

The staff in general were amazing — fast service, spotless place, and such a welcoming atmosphere.

Highly recommend this spot to everyone visiting London, it’s a must! 🌟

This spot is just a short walk from Liverpool Street Station, so the location is great and very central.

We had our Sunday morning breakfast here and really enjoyed it. At 8:45 there were barely any tables taken; by 10 most were full.

The selection is big enough to suit pretty much everyone. We especially appreciated the wide range of vegetarian options and found the “sausages” super tasty. Hash browns were honestly the best we’ve ever had. Pancakes were fluffy, though very filling.
The baked beans, however, weren’t to our taste – honestly, we’d even prefer the canned ones :D.. But of course, taste varies!

The staff were relatively kind. There are only two bathrooms, both plastered with stickers and little notes from strangers, which is a really fun touch. Cleanliness could be improved a bit, though.

One thing to keep in mind: there’s an “optional” 12.5% service charge added to the bill. So, in my opinion, there’s really no need to tip extra if that‘s already included (as a tourist, I always find this kind of pre-set charge a bit questionable).

reviews.text:
A very pleasant and atmospheric place. The staff is friendly and helpful.
This was our third time there and we were pleased again. All the food was delicious and freshly prepared. We were a large group, and everything was served at the same time and kept hot.
There's an excellent selection of juicy burgers and a variety of sets. The portions are really large, which justifies the prices. The meat mix was simply amazing, delicious, and melts in your mouth. To make eating the hearty burgers more comfortable, everyone is given a decent-sized cloth napkin, which is really convenient.
On one of our visits, there was a live Latin American band playing, which really set the festive mood for the day.
We've definitely become regulars.
Thank you so much!

I ordered the Doomsday Device burger/sandwich which tasted pretty good but the over-the-top greasiness ruined the experience for me, unfortunately. Loved the fries and the Chocolate Malt Shake though.

The service was super slow and we were a big group and had to wait for over 30 minutes to finally place our orders. We sat outside and the ambience was very good with the outside heating on.

I came here with a bigger group, and even though we were polite and easy customers, the staff were just straight-up rude, shouting across the place and making the whole atmosphere unpleasant. It was too loud to have a proper chat, and the place was so cramped you couldn’t even put your bag down without being told off.

The food was just as bad. I ordered a spicy burger, which came covered in a ridiculous amount of jalapeños and habaneros. I usually handle spicy food with no problem, but this one made me feel actually unwell. My stomach and throat were burning, and I even felt sick the next day. Safe to say this completely destroyed my appetite.

Overall, really not worth it. Unfriendly staff, uncomfortable setting, and overpriced food. Wouldn’t recommend at all.

On trend Mid-Western / Southern American food joint in Hoxton Square, Old Street. Plays some country music and a relaxed welcoming atompshere. The burgers are huge and dirty (in a good way). About the right price point. Service was good, maybe not the warmest, but perfectly fine. One of the better and more bankable food options in that area

It's dude food.  We ended up here accidentally because Odyssey on the other side of the square cancelled our reservation at the last minute because I am on crutches so couldn't  make it down the stairs to a basement table.
Staff are all very kind and helpful but professionalism and knowledge about the menu varies.  We both got baskets where I got the platter with wings and my companion got the smoked brisket.  Proteins were all well executed.  My wings were deep fried but not greasy, the brisket was tasty and tender.  However I hated the accompaniments like greasy chips, and slaw smothered in copious amounts of mayo.  I didn't even try the greasy looking Texas toast.
If I ever come back I will order a starter of wings and a side caesar to avoid all the greasy accompaniments.

The service and atmosphere was fantastic, the food was also great if chosen correctly.

On Valentines night we chose the whole roasted lobster and stuffed saddle of lamb, the lobster was perfect but the lamb was stuffed alright, stuffed with too much and hardly any lamb.

It tasted nice, but stick with the duck amd waffle. The lamb was disappointing but everything else was top notch.

We chose this restaurant to celebrate our anniversary on Sunday, and I’m so glad we did. From the moment we arrived, the service was amazing, friendly, attentive, and welcoming throughout.
The food was outstanding, and the views alone are worth every penny. It’s definitely on the pricier side, but for a special occasion, I would absolutely recommend it. You’re paying not just for the food, but for the whole experience.
That said, I didn’t order an alcoholic drink because of the prices. While I understand that London is expensive and that this place reflects the quality and overall experience it offers, I do think they could consider offering more affordable drink options and focusing the higher price point on the food instead.
A lovely touch was the complimentary dessert they provided for our anniversary, it made the evening feel even more special.
Overall, we had a wonderful time, and I’m really happy I chose this restaurant to celebrate our second anniversary. It was a memorable experience.

Such a vibe being up on the 40th floor. We got super lucky and scored an absolutely perfect window seat with view of the Tower Bridge, which honestly made the whole experience for us.
Tip on seating:
We booked the "festive brunch" which was at a normal table. It seems like window seats are mostly reserved for pairs, while bigger groups usually get placed in the middle. If you're a group of more than two, try for the "counter table", there seem to be a few tables with a nice view.
​The food was good. I also tried orange wine for the first time. The waiter was so kind and took the time to explain the tropical flavor profile to me.
If you're veggie: there aren't many vegetarian options on the set menu we had, so check the à la carte if you have the option.
Overall: the service felt a little rushed at times, could be also because it was a public holiday. In my opinion, it’s worth the money if you get a window seat. Without the view, it might feel a bit "meh," but with it, it's a highlight.

We had a wonderful evening celebrating my birthday at Duck & Waffle. The food and cocktails were excellent, and the atmosphere made the night even more special. A special thanks to Sommelier Luis, who took great care of us throughout the evening. His professionalism, warm hospitality, and great recommendations truly elevated our experience. Everything about the night was delightful, and it’s definitely a place we will happily return to. Highly recommended for a memorable evening in London!

Such an incredible atmosphere and welcome. It was like being transported into another place entirely. Our waitress Tilly was so friendly, welcoming and attentive. She had a lovely chat with us while we paid and made the experience even better!

The food was unique and tasted incredible. I would definitely go back here on my next visit!

A really great place to play chess on Tuesday evenings in a fun social environment! It does get very busy so you need to arrive early or bide your time to get a table. The atmosphere is really fun and everyone is super friendly, it’s quite casual and there are a variety of levels of players from beginners to experts.

Eclectic place, it’s a cafe / restaurant in the day and a bar at night, I like modern retro industrial style, food is good, rapid service and friendly staff. Good location in the heart of brick lane market area.

Delicious breakfast with an amazing vibe. Staff were friendly and food came out really quick! We came early on a Sunday.
Only hiccup was that the coffee and tea were a bit watery.
fun chill spot. they have great coffee and fun events at night throughout the week like chess night and “bring your own vinyl” night

Perfect spot for everything! Great food, amazing decorations and lovely staff. Loved the vibe and the variety they offer, being a café in the daytime and a bar at nighttime, even bringing dj's in! Super place and 100% recommend it!

The lemon-cured beef salad was incredible. Then we hesitated about the Pho. We asked our waiter, Diego, who gave an excellent recommendation with the garlicky pho. We had never tatsted this kîd of Pho before and it was a really good surprise. The atmosphere of the restaurant is nice, not too crowded (friday night around 8pm) and the staff was lovely! Thank you Diego, we'll be back!

super Vietnamese authentic restaurant. love the local chains in London and this is added to my favorites list, had the bunbo hue which is super authentic and had all the meats along with the pho which was good. I think it was pretty decent but the bunbo hue overshown, and had the crispy crab parcel which was so delicious and like tasty from the first bite to the end and had the right sauce and crabbyness to it would definitely come back

I’ve been coming here for over 20 years as I work just around the corner. The menu has only ever become more interesting and the food better and better in that time. Today I had the £19:95 set lunch menu with the ‘piggy’ aubergine starter and Spring Bowl as a main course. The latter was improved over last time I had it, with lots of fresh raw herbs and greens and excellent crispy rolls on top. I really recommend Cay Tre for lunch: the service is brisk, the food is fresh, and very delicious.

Amazing experience. Foods are wholesome and absolutely delectable. I tried the shrimp spring rolls and grilled pork vermicelli, both were flavorful and satisfying.
The staff are friendly, especially Jules, who made a delicious drink and provided excellent service. The restaurant is clean, neat, and incredibly cozy.
I highly recommend stopping by if you’re looking for an authentic taste of Vietnamese cuisine.

As a Vietnamese living in London, Cay Tre is one of my top favourite Vietnamese restaurants. They have a wide ranges of Vietnamese food, the quality is really good and some dishes are close to home. The Cay Tre at Hoxton is smaller than the one in Soho, but still quite cosy vibe and good quality, albeit smaller menu than the other branch. I’d always recommend friends to visit at least once!

reviews.text:
We had such a lovely time at this restaurant. Food was delicious and the drinks were really good too!
Flaviya was an absolute star - we didn’t have a booking but she squeezed us in on such a busy night. She ensured we were well looked after and she was so lovely to talk to. Thank you for a wonderful Saturday night. Definitely be coming bak thanks to Flaviya!

We enjoyed their Michelin starred popup from LA - Pastabar. Menu is £59pp. You get starter each, share 2 mains (pizza, pasta) and dessert each. The lobster pasta was one of the best pastas of my life. The bone marrow and anchovy pizza was different but it worked so well together.
I’d prefer a more traditional dessert than granita but it was refreshing. The cocktails from this menu weren’t strong. I’d prefer quieter ambiance for this special menu but otherwise good.

I went to Pizza East for their famous Lasagne. I thought it was lovely but it did miss something, more spice and more heat, the middle was not as hot as the edges and a spicey kick would have gave it the 5 stars. The server was brilliant, dressed very well, energetic and even gave me recommendations. The atmosphere was mellow, good music almost comfortable enough for me to undo my belt and kick off my shoes. Great experience! I recommend.

One of the best pizzas I’ve had. I went for the San Daniele with tomato sauce. The base was perfectly thin and crispy, and the tomato sauce was fresh and light. We also ordered Calabrian fried potato’s, which were very nice, and calamari, which tasted fresh but we felt the pieces were very small. We were attended to by 3 staff members; two of who were lovely , but we were not impressed with the other. They appeared to have a cold and really shouldn’t have been at work. All in all, I would defo back.

Thank you Flavia for serving all of us tonight, even tho we were a large table she made sure to take care of us. Genuinely never seen a more happy server. Made our night, definitely recommend to everyone pizzaeast is lovely.

Dishoom definitely lives up to the hype. We were a group of five and didn’t have a reservation, but we were able to join the line and got a table in about 45 minutes. The best part was that they offer complimentary drinks while you wait, which made the experience much more enjoyable.

The food was absolutely delicious and worth the wait. My favourites were the lamb biryani and the lamb chops — both were incredibly flavourful and perfectly cooked.

Top tier. The food was incredible, the service was excellent - friendly, informed, and prompt. One of our group members had a unique allergy (onions) and the staff worked diligently to highlight the menu items she could eat.

All around phenomenal time. Highly recommend for locals and travelers alike. As mentioned by a previous reviewer, the staff are also happy and seem to enjoy their job which elevates the experience in my book.

Would recommend: New Keema Pau, Lamb Biryani, Garlic Naan, Murgh Malai, and Raita

Visited the Shoreditch franchise today and it was nothing but the best! The staff is unbelievably friendly yet professional. Can’t expect this in heart of London anywhere nowadays. Sat in the Veranda section which is outside the main wing of the restaurant and the ambience is next level. Comfy sofas with low table or choices of high table as per own choice. Food is excellent and service is prompt. Kids friendly and wheelchair accessible. Would definitely recommend Serene who is the host ( supervisor ) who plays an inevitable part in running the busy operation so smoothly.

1 hour wait at 5:30PM on a December Friday. Excellent Indian food in a cozy and eclectic setting. You sit in cushy armchairs as you share saucy dishes across a coffee table. Such a fun place to eat among good company. We ordered the fried okra, black daal, ruby chicken, mattar paneer, lamb chops, an order of rice and multiple orders of garlic naan. They were all do delicious and full of flavours and spices. I would happily order them all over again.

Lovely and very knowledgeable staff. A very large menu to choose from with a lot of detail both for food and drinks. The interior has such a great vibe. You can tell a lot of attention and effort went into creating the atmosphere. All staff were super lovely and the manager came around to each table which was a lovely attentive touch. The food itself was great. It was my first time eating at dishoom and I was far from disappointed. Each dish was full of flavour. However, I found the naan to be a bit lacking. I've had better naan from local curry shops. Definitely not bad but not the best naan I've had, which is the reason for the 4 stars on food. The desserts were great, highly recommend the rice pudding! Will definitely come again.

name: Sheba Restaurant - Awarded Best Curry House In UK
name_normalised: sheba restaurant awarded best curry house in uk

reviews.text:
We booked Sheba two months in advance to meet a friend I hadn’t seen in a while. We both love curry and regularly eat at curry houses all over the UK, from Leeds and Bradford to London and beyond, so we know what good food looks and tastes like. Unfortunately, this was nowhere near it.

The naan breads were shockingly small, around five inches in diameter and perfectly circular. They looked more like mini supermarket flatbreads than proper restaurant naan.

For mains, we ordered a garlic chilli chicken and a lamb naga. These are two completely different styles of curry and should taste very distinct. Instead, both sauces tasted almost identical. Same base, same flavour profile, just different meat dropped in. The meat in both dishes was cut into tiny pieces and did not taste great quality.

Starters were around £10 each. We had lamb chops and half a chicken. When they arrived, they were served on tiny little four or five inch plates that genuinely looked like IKEA side plates.

The half chicken was basically one chicken leg with zero tandoori flavour, just plain chicken with a bit of salad on the side. We had specifically asked for lots of chopped green chillies. Instead, the kitchen sent out about five whole green chillies, unchopped. What exactly are you meant to do with whole chillies on top of a plain chicken leg?

The lamb chops were dry and looked like they had been sitting around for a while. They were passable, but nothing special and certainly not worth the price.

To be fair, the pints of Kingfisher were good. Fresh, cold, clean taps and reasonably priced. Drinks were the only positive.

The total bill was over £100. We paid in full, including service charge, and did not send anything back because we were hungry, but it was a huge let down, especially given the booking and the occasion.

If you are heading to Brick Lane, I would strongly recommend Bengal Village instead. Sheba was a massive disappointment and I would not return.

I want to wipe my memories from eating this food, not exactly sure how there could be disappointing. Indian food in London, had the popular dishes. Had the menthi lamb which was mediocre at best but outshone the rest, with the tandoori chicken which was super dry, the mint sauce that didn't resemble any kind of chutney I've ever seen on Earth, and the samosas which were like trader Joe's air fried pieces, and the super sweet mango lassi. and the naan was old and dry too, super disappointing but service was decent nevertheless

Came here after seeing 30% off on The Fork - get the feeling “awarded best curry house in uk” is just the full name of the restaurant rather than any kind of certificate. My local takeaway in Manchester blows this place out of the water, the cheek to call it best curry house in the UK - had the jalfrezi was underwhelming and incredibly mild, bland even - karahi was an improvement but still nothing to write home about, chapatis were beyond dry genuinely think they were made from drywall, peshwari naan was enjoyable but it’s hard to mess a peshwari naan up. Main issue was the incredibly tense aura in the restaurant, felt if i breathed too hard i’d be sentenced to death, with waiters being quite rude and disdainful that I was using a 30% off offer? which the service charge cancelled out regardless?? Would not recommend, food would be passable if the atmosphere was better, but atmosphere is so tense I cannot recommend

I had an excellent experience at Sheba Restaurant on Brick Lane. They offer a wide selection of Pakistani, Indian, and Bengali dishes, and every dish was bursting with authentic flavors. The food was fresh, well-prepared, and absolutely delicious.

The service was just as impressive – the staff were friendly, attentive, and made me feel very welcome. The atmosphere was warm and inviting, making it the perfect place to enjoy a great meal.

If you’re looking for a restaurant on Brick Lane that serves amazing South Asian food with top-notch service, I highly recommend Sheba Restaurant. I’ll definitely be visiting again!

Don’t order from this place!! Disappointed doesn’t even cover it. Ordered delivery this evening (6/12) and it was honestly the worst curry I’ve had In my life. Lamb buhna (pictured) was just oil and water and a grey colour that doesn’t give me any confidence in its safety. The other curry The Lamb ladyfinger, the sauce in that had also completely split. The whole meal was completely inedible.

We had a wonderful experience dining here. The service was outstanding — the staff  Don & Joana were attentive, friendly, and made us feel genuinely welcome from start to finish. The atmosphere was warm and inviting, creating the perfect setting for a relaxed and enjoyable meal.
The food was absolutely top-notch. Every dish was beautifully presented and packed with flavour, clearly made with care and high-quality ingredients. It’s rare to find a place where the service, atmosphere, and food all come together so perfectly.
I would highly recommend this restaurant and will definitely be returning!

Thank you from Lisa  G x

Our first visit as a group to the Cinnamon Kitchen was very special. The food was exceptional and the service excellent. Ash seemed to be looking after us very well. Every one of us had a beautiful meal. We truly had the best time. Think our group of school friends will be returning. It’s not often we all agree but we’re 💯 in agreement to revisit the Cinnamon Kitchen soon

Great experience at Cinnamon Kitchen! The starters were absolutely amazing—full of flavour and beautifully presented. The only minor letdown was the lack of a chicken curry in the mains, but everything else was delicious and the ambience was lovely. Would definitely visit again!

Excellent lunch with my Mum thanks to a present from my wonderful son for Mother’s Day. Rupa looked after us (as did others who were great) and she was brilliant. Advising us on which dishes to choose, as well as making the most devine cocktails (Cinnamon Bellini and leaf). Everything was delicious, fragrant and Devine. Service was brilliant and a fantastic lunch with my mum. We had the set lunch and it was excellent. We would go back again.

We held our baby shower at Cinnamon Kitchen and were extremely happy with the experience. The decor was beautiful – we booked the upper terrace and it was covered in flowers and plants, which created a lovely atmosphere. Although it was January and the weather was cooler, the heaters and lamps kept everyone comfortable.

The food was excellent. We selected a set menu and all of our guests thoroughly enjoyed it. The staff and particularly Shatarupa was also fantastic, very friendly, attentive, and regularly checked in to see if we needed anything.

I would definitely recommend Cinnamon Kitchen for events, and I’ll absolutely be considering it again for any future celebrations.

I can’t recommend the Horse and Groom highly enough for any private celebration — they truly exceeded all expectations!

I recently hosted my 50th birthday there, and the entire experience was outstanding from beginning to end. The team went out of their way to make the evening feel special and completely stress-free.

The venue itself is ideal: great location, plenty of space, warm atmosphere, and beautifully arranged for a private party. Every member of staff — from security to the bar  — were professional, friendly, and genuinely attentive, ensuring all of our guests felt welcomed and well looked after.

The vibe on the night was fantastic. The sound system is excellent, and the fact that it’s included in the room-hire price (along with fast, efficient staff and security) is a huge bonus. It all came together to create a truly unforgettable celebration.

If you’re planning an event, the Horse and Groom is an easy choice. You won’t be disappointed!

A brilliant pub with an even better team. We hosted a work quiz night upstairs in the Horse & Groom and Neil and team made everything so easy. Nothing was too much trouble in the planning and the bar staff were incredible throughout the evening - and they make a great aperol! The perfect space. If I could give 6 stars, I would!

I go to Unique Rhythm event every 3rd Saturday in the month. It is brilliant, several DJs playing soulful house music. If you want to have a good time surrounded by good people, good music and have a good dance it's the place to go.

We held a work event on the first floor with about 75 people. It was a great space and everyone had a good time. We had a DJ, the sound system and lights are great. The bar staff were friendly and efficient. We ordered pizzas which were all tasty. Recommend booking for your event.

Unique Rhythm Soulful House Parties are the best. Fantastic Djs who really get the crowd going. The music is outstanding and the atmosphere is super.
Never the same old music, always something wonderfully different. The Djs interact with the crowd and clearly love what they do.
I absolutely recommend this event, never any trouble and I always feel so safe.
