reviews.text:
We booked the Loft at The Light Bar this weekend to host our wedding drinks and couldn’t be happier with the top tier service we received!
Great communications and explanation throughout. Excellent food & bar service and very grateful for the little extra mile they went on countless details of hosting a wedding party night for 90 approx people.
They provided ample amount of the amenities needed, kept me updated throughout a smooth running night. Fantastic staff and service. Thanks team!

I was there once and I liked the experience! We were 3 girls, ended up at The Light Bar on a Friday evening. We ordered cocktails and I loved mine! The service was good, the staff is nice and the space is spacious. I do think that it might be also a good venue for celebrations or events. There was a live DJ playing and he really nailed it. Although it is a bit loudy, I really liked the place and you can still find a place to chill and hear each other somewhere upstairs. Recommended!

The Light Bar hosted my VIP Dinner for women in my professional network in London. From the moment of booking, the staff were so helpful and communication and planning was spot on. We did a group set menu and the food was spectacular, so delicious and very generous servings with wonderful fresh, rich flavours. They kindly catered to dietary requirements and the service was impeccable - they really took care of us and we were all super impressed. They accommodated us moving to an outdoor table given it was such a beautiful balmy June evening and it was truly magical to relax and connect. Would absolutely recommend it for any corporate or personal event - it was an amazing venue.

Along with cocktails, the group set menu was absolutely spectacular starting with burrata and peppers, salmon fennel citrus salad, trout and crème fraiche, flatbreads both plain and topped with olive and tomato, and crispy chickpea hummus. Next came shared mains - delicious hispy cabbage on ratatouille, basil pesto baked orzo with rocket and Parmesan, and a baby chicken with gravy and greens. And of course we squeezed in the mountain of crispy churros with chocolate pots because dessert obviously goes into another tube.

I was truly blown away by the fresh flavour-packed dishes, perfect location, and wonderful service. I’m still dreaming of that heavenly trout dip…

I’m very disappointed with my recent visit. There were many empty tables available, yet we were refused a Sunday roast because we were seated in the bar area, which staff said was only for “nibbles.”

I was told I could order something small like fries, but not a full meal. This made very little sense given that the dining area clearly had space. It felt unnecessarily restrictive and not very customer-friendly.

If there are empty tables, customers should be able to order from the full menu or at least be offered the option to move to a dining table. The current setup is confusing and frustrating, and it really affected our experience.

I hope this can be reviewed so future customers aren’t turned away in the same way.

the burger is decent but not really really good. the menu got limited choices. service is alright but it took a while to get a pint from them. dj music is a bit too loud at dinner time. dont really know the positioning of this restaurant / bar. it is below average if you consider it as a restaurant. it is ok if you treat it as a bar. probably not visit again in the near future.

An absolute gem in the heart of London.
The staff welcomes every guest with warmth and lovely smiles. Great ambience, blending South India with subtle modernity. Authentic food, wide menu, great tasting finger licking food, that isn't very pricey either.
Their kufies are a must have.

Everything about our visit was fantastic - from the warm welcome to the beautifully presented dishes. Our creative starters, rich curries and perfectly balanced desserts were full of flavour and clearly made with care.

A special thank you to Sharron, who was incredibly kind and attentive throughout our meal. Her genuine hospitality made our lunch feel extra special.

Highly recommend this restaurant for anyone looking for great food, a cozy atmosphere, and outstanding service!

Had a wonderful experience here! We didn’t have a booking, but they still found us a table right away and were incredibly accommodating. It was my birthday, and they truly made the day feel special. Our server was new, but you would never have known it—she did a brilliant job and provided such warm, attentive service. Overall, the customer service was excellent and made our visit memorable. Highly recommend!
Great food. The service was great very welcoming. Nice layout and design which gave it a nice atmosphere.

Fantastic South Indian food. We were a group 8 on a Sunday night at 10pm. They had dosa, idly and biryani. The idly dosas were great. Sambar was excellent, Chutneys full of flavor. Refreshing Indian flavored drinks. Overall a great restaurant with excellent service. Highly recommend if you are in London and craving some authentic South Indian food.
Had a 5pm dinner last night after the theatre - lobster and steak (valentines special) and service and food were excellent !!! Would recommend it as we’ve been a few times and it’s always great

Food was really good! However, the service was not great. We had a reservation at 8pm for 10 people, unfortunately 4 people cancelled last minute so we ended up being just 6. 3 of us were there at 8o clock and 3 arrived at 8:15. Around 8:10, someone that seemed like the manager or person in charge, asked us if we were ordering food and if the rest of the people were coming, we told him they were arriving in a minute and he proceeded to be incredibly rude saying that the kitchen closed at 8:30pm (online it’s said the kitchen was open until 10pm, I wouldn’t have made a reservation for 8pm if the kitchen was closing at 8:30) and if we didn’t order now we wouldn’t be able to eat, I told him that we had just arrived and he asked “wasn’t your reservation at 8? It’s 8:15! You need or order now!” I was honestly SHOCKED at the way he spoke to us. My friend told him we were going to wait for the other 3 people and in less than 2minutes they were there. We ordered our food in the next 10min and they served us. The food was good, but honestly I was there celebrating my birthday with my friends and being spoke to that way was incredibly rude and unnecessary. If your kitchen closes at 8:30 you should let people know about the right kitchen closing time, especially if you’re accepting a dinner reservation at 8pm, and it being a cocktail bar we were having some drinks first and we’re talking with no rush.
I understand that sometimes information online is not the same as reality, but you don’t have to be rude or miss treat people to get your point across, he could have just told us about the kitchen on arrival or just by having a different attitude.

Great little cocktail bar with a really nice vibe. The drinks were well made and the staff were friendly and attentive. The atmosphere was relaxed but lively, perfect for catching up with friends or going on a date. Would definitely come back to try more cocktails!

I have been coming to the drift for years and it never disappoints! Duck & waffle and Sushisamba get all the attention being on the top floor of the building, but people forget about this hidden gem on the ground floor! Food is always delicious, service is always great and the music & vibes are excellent.
I took my best friend for bottomless brunch and we loved it. I really liked that they had bottomless aperol spritz as an option. The service was great and they even gave us a complimentary dessert with “Congratulations” written on it because we were celebrating my friend’s engagement.
We stayed after brunch for extra drinks in the bar area and Gustavo made sure we were looked after, recommending loads of lovely cocktails to us!
I will definitely be back, and I’d highly recommend The Drift for your next lunch, brunch, dinner or /special occasion!

Our server Moni was so wonderful! It was my first bottomless brunch where I didn’t have to look around for a drink! The staff were so attentive, the food was great and the music , atmosphere so fab!!!!!x

Great atmosphere and amazing food! The service was fast and the portions were very satisfactory. I had the half eggs benedict and half potatoes and the pancakes with lemon cream, fruits and maple syrup. Also cappuccino was very good. Staff was very friendly and attentive! The atmosphere was calm and it was easy to talk and relax! Overall would definitely recommend and definitely will visit again!!!

Had an amazing experience here at the breakfast club. The food was AMAZING! Was honestly so impressed. The servers were fantastic, very attentive, helpful and friendly. The atmosphere was lovely and the interior of the restaurant is so cute. Would definitely recommend!

1 white americano & bean shakshuka with 2 extra eggs & chorizo £27.00  (extras - 2 x eggs £3 and Chorzo £2.50)
First time here on a Sunday monring 8.45am
The lighting isnt great inside, its particularily dark/dimly lit and in the corner where my table was located and I had to use my phone torch to read the menu. Im not sure if the lights are on dimmer swtiches but they could definatley do with turning up. The decor is also a bit drab and not very uplifitng or insipring.
I ordeed the Anvars Turkish Eggs and an Americano, though I was told a few munites later that my food order wasnt available today, so i opted instead for the Bean Shakshuka with 2 extrra eggs and chorizo.
My order arrived swiftly, yet it was cold in places and just tepid in others, so it was sent back for a replacement. Obviously microwaved from a pot but not temprature checked/probed before serving.
My replacement also arrived fairly swiftly and was this time hot, though clearly microwave hot !
I will also add the portions are not very generous. My shakshuka was served on a very shallow plate, almost like a sandwhich plate with a lip, a very thin layer of the shakshuka only just covered the surface of the place . I felt as if the toast that come with it as the accompaniment was the main feature as that dominated the plate, where it should be the other way around.
The waiting staff are very polite,attentive and helpful despite the food not being up to much.
To summerise I would say very overpriced for average food.
I dont mind paying good money for food but it has to be decent quality, served hot, and enough of it to make me feel statisfied that ive just eaten.
There are far better places localy to eat for the same or maybe even slighty less where you will find better sized portions and served piping hot. And the lights switched on !

I thought it was a good place with a good atmosphere. I thought the food was pretty good, too. I had the shakshuka, I prefer a bit more spice and usually have it without beans but it was decent. My friends really liked the vibe and the food they ordered, and one of my friends really liked the service. So although I found it to be an average brunch place with normal service, I took their input into consideration for this slightly above average rating.
Manuel swapped our table to more comfortable booth after we were served to different table which was very kind. Good service and good on Sunday afternoon, we will come back again. Thank you :)

Went for reef beef bubble January deal with my friend. The menu provided isn’t very accurate of what’s been served.
The steak is a rump steak instead of sirloin like in the menu, both steak (medium rare) and lobster are a bit of dry. I had add on giant grilled prawn which is just one medium sized prawn and bit dry as well (and less fresh)
Instead of a pint of Asahi 0.0% they only give you the bottle (330ml).
Overall average experience for the price we paid, would expect more for a nice looking place like this.

What a fab place. We took our sausage dog and her 7 favourite humans and the service was flexible, professional, warm but very unimposing. The food was delicious and liked by everyone. Drinks were of a high standard and it's a very attractive place. We all loved it thank you

I liked everything about the Cinnamon kitchen. Large atmosphere but still felt cosy. The waitresses were knowledgeable and friendly. The food was served  fresh and cooked to perfection.
The duo musicians who came late to play guitar and saxophone were also super. The only problem is that they played toooooo loud that i couldn't hear my friends voice.
I think the music was too loud for the restaurants atmosphere.
Overall i would definitely recommend Cinnamon kitchen
and I would go again. Hopefully the music is a little lower!.

Fabulous location. Absolutely stunning setting for an evening dinner with friends or a cozy couples date, or even just a drink or a cocktail. Gorgeous outdoor area with the heaters, seeds, blanket/throws, all under a beautiful atrium. Menu pretty decent and mid range. Reasonable prices. All food came out pretty good and fair price. Dog friendly. Would definitely go again as a nice place to meet up with the girls for lunch/dinner/drink drinks.

We went to Devonshire Terrace for dinner tonight and we had the unfortunate experience of seeing mice in the restaurant. The meal and environment were nice, however we saw a mouse a few feet away from our table while we were having dessert. We told a staff member about the unsanitary issue, who raised it to the manager, but no action was taken. We were not offered any compensation or apologies, and the staff member told us that other customers had a similar experience and management took no action.
As this is so unsanitary, I cannot recommend this place and hope they address the pest issue.

Took my friend here for his farewell dinner in London and we had a great meal. The sirloin steak was charred on the outside and juicy in the middle, cooked exactly right. The beef dripping chips were thick‑cut, golden and addictive, while the beef dripping fries were crisp and impossible to stop picking at. The mash with gravy was smooth, buttery and comforting, and the macaroni cheese was creamy, gooey and easily the side that stole the show. Friendly service and a relaxed atmosphere made it a really nice evening.

Wonderful, wonderful steak. Pictured is the chateaubriand, cooked medium rare and absolutely delicious - the bérnaise sauce was a wonderful addition to the gorgeous texture. Service is friendly, and the setting is also very nice.

Always a safe choice when looking for a restaurant. Hawksmoor never lets you down, and I have been to alot of them.

Finally got to try the Big Matt, was nice, but now I have tried it I won't need have another. Il stick to the steak.

Service was good on the night, real good buzz for atmosphere considering it was a Tuesday.

Reliable, but never amazing.

Food is very nice, lots of Steak and dessert choice so there is something for everyone :)

Unfortunately we had to wait a while to be seated although we had a reservation, but the waiter made up for this by giving us some free food. They also forgot that we were there for a birthday so we had to remind them which felt a bit awkward.. The lighting is also a little too dim.

We visited for a family meal in October. The cocktails, wine, food was fantastic, you'll defo leave feeling full! As a vegetarian, it can be difficult in meaty places but they still offer options. My fellow guests love coming here for steak and is one of their favourites / go to. The service was exceptional, always topping up, attentive and nothing was too long of a wait. The lady that served us even advised me what I could / couldn't eat on the table as we were having sharers and even offered alternatives they could make for me which was thoughtful. Only minor thing I'd say is I'd personally prefer ice cream with the sticky toffee pudding!

Lovely service and amazing food. Steak is always brilliant but the sides are wonderful too especially the spinach! The sundae dessert also blew me away, I thought it would be way too sweet but it was lovely (shared between two otherwise might’ve been too much)

Generally very good, lives up to the name and reputation, with nice cuts of meat cooked well. Seafood starters also nice, freshly prepared. Sides and sauces complement the meat dishes nicely and the environment is lively, typical for a City steakhouse.

A good location for a business dinner or after work with friends/colleagues.

Excellent evening with the lads. Food was excellent as always! Steaks clocked perfectly. Service was a little slow, but Eric stepped in and bossed it from then on.

Very accommodating and looked after us very well!

We took my 15 year old cousin here as he loves steak (cooking and eating) and I've had good experiences in the past at the Mayfair location.

Prices are, like many steak places, eye watering. It was a Saturday evening and the restaurant was quiet, even when we were leaving at 8pm.

I don't object to paying for good quality food and service but I must say, we got a very mixed bag with this place.

On arrival, we were seated in a nice booth at the front.. Our server was helpful and pleasant, we were offered drinks and menus immediately, and shown the customary raw meat selection.

Interestingly most of the starters are seafood based (prawn, crab, tuna) which is a problem if you have a slightly picky teenager with you. He had the bread basket to himself (which you're charged for, which in and of itself, I find astonishing). Over 30 years of going to all kinds of higher end restaurants and this is the only time I've been charged for bread other than specialised bread baskets. Last year's teenager birthday meal was The Ivy, the year before The Savoy Grill. On neither occasion did either restaurant charge for the standard, pre-meal bread. In fact, the Savoy provided a second basket for the teenager free of charge.

To start I had the prawn tempura and the other guest had the burrata. The burrata was good quality and tasty. The prawns were generous but I found the creamy sauce and batter a sickly combination. I felt in needed more citrus, sharpness.

I ordered the sirloin as my main, teen had the Australian Ribeye and the other guest has the fillet. We ordered fries, chips and green beans to accompany alongside 2 x peppercorn sauce and 1 x Stilton.

The sirloin was beautifully cooked and very tasty. As was the Fillet. However, the ribeye was underdone and the Stilton sauce tasted only of beef gravy. We sent both back. The ribeye was refunded and the Stilton sauce left unimproved and replaced with a bernaise (at our request) in the end.

On taking the ribeye away the manager (? I assume, she never introduced herself) asked if we wanted another. We said no as we were half way through out meals. She did not return to follow up or establish what the outcome of the complaint would be. And she did not apologise.

Super disappointing.

Our waiter was very good, though, and apologetic. They did provide a Birthday sundae for the teenager but we opted not to order anything further.

In the end, the ribeye had been removed from our bill, as had the sauce.

Its worth noting that this place adds a 15% service charge. I once again implore all visitors to London restaurants to ask for service charges to be removed.

Restaurants that charge £40 for their cheapest steak and £9 for each side order should not be expecting guests to plump up staff wages. We have a living wage in the UK and, whilst I continue to (and encourage others to) tip for very good service, I don't believe in the ever growing trend on foisting service charging on customers.

And 15% is ludicrous.

A disappointment in the end, especially as it was the teenager who didn't enjoy his steak and it was his birthday. Won't be returning.

We were alone in the restaurant and had to wait for drinks when the meat was already on the table (the bartender was too busy talking), and then the waiters forgot about us and didn't come over.
The meat was of good quality, but the taste was ruined by the burning due to the cooking method.

The dessert and tart-tart were delicious

We needed a table for 8 following our son's graduation at the Barbican Centre. I had seen The Old Fountain online and the menu looked good. They were able to accommodate us, probably as it was early evening on a Monday. We had a great time and were looked after very well by the friendly staff. We started with a load of delicious Momos. Everyone enjoyed their food, which ranged from different burgers, to fish and chips, and an amazingly tasty curry in a pot with mashed potato (it was spectacular!!!).
We were sat near to the kitchen and were able to compliment the chef personally! The wine was lovely and there was a great selection of ales, beers and ciders. We definitely want to return.

Stopped by for a quick drink. First visit. Nice enough place, old pub feel and vibe. Nice choice of drinks at usual London prices. Service was friendly. Sadly the glasses looked like the glass wash machine needs a change of detergent or rinse aid because they were very cloudy, the photo of the glasses on the back bar just about shows this. Overall a nice place.

We had our Christmas do at Old Fountain as it's one of our favourite pubs and it was such a brilliant and well-organised evening. Alex and the team were incredibly accommodating with our big group and made us feel well looked after all night. Thanks to all the team, couldn't recommend it enough.
Class beer selection, food was amazing (incredible Nepalese cooking way better than your standard pub stuff) and a really unpretentious atmosphere.

Went in for “just one pint” and somehow left three hours later than planned emotionally invested in the pub dog and made two new pals Dave and Sally.

The food was wicked, the beer selection is solid, and I love that it’s dog friendly, seeing a few happy pups around somehow makes the whole place feel even more like a proper local. A super friendly gaff.
The pints was spot on, cold, crisp, and poured with the kind of care usually reserved for newborns babies.

Also worth mentioning that the atmosphere / music choice was great,  not to forget the darts board and the cool rooftop seating area! Defo the kind of place where you come in for one and end up staying far longer than planned ( like I did )

Would absolutely return.
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

The best Sunday roast I ever had!
I had a pork belly and it was absolutely amazing! Yorkshire, veges, chutney , pork it was delicious!
The place looked a bit random at first, but we went upstairs to sit on the rooftop terrace and it was a great atmosphere, staff friendly and attentive and the food amazing, so would definitely recommend it for sure.

name: Mint Leaf London
address: Bank, 12 Angel Ct, London EC2R 7HB, UK

reviews.text:
Very nice ambiance, impeccable service and succulent food. We celebrated a birthday here with family and we had an absolutely wonderful time at Mint Leaf, London.

Aloo Tikki Chaat, Paneer Tikka & Chicken Tikka were the best starters we have had. The mojitos and lassi were delicious to go with the starters.

For mains we had Bhindi, Koftas, Daal Bukhara & Lamb Nihari. Their garlic naan and butter naan were crunchy, buttery and delicious.

Thanks to the staff for very attentive and impeccable service.

Had an incredible first visit to Mint Leaf and was truly impressed. The food is authentic, flavorful, and absolutely delicious. The chaat starters were amazing, and although the veg seekh kebab wasn’t our favorite, the main course more than made up for it — the jackfruit kofta was outstanding and the dal makhani was very good, paired perfectly with coriander and butter naan. The food we ordered was too much for two of us but we managed to finish almost everything as it was quite delicious.
The ambience is pleasant, we were seated immediately without a reservation, and the staff was friendly and accommodating. Overall a 10/10 experience.
highly recommended!

Mint Leaf London was such a great surprise in the heart of the City. The space feels grand and modern, with a polished atmosphere that still keeps the warmth of traditional Indian dining. Great portions, thoughtful presentation, and a lovely setting for dinner or even a special occasion. Would definitely return.
Loved the place. Great location, food was nice and it’s handy for business meetings, events, team get togethers, client dinners. Of course that have a great bar too and plenty of cocktails I believe!
Lovely food and great atmosphere. Only critic is when we complained about the naans being cold the waiter got defensive and didn’t apologise. It’s a shame really as food ambiance was lovely

name: LOUNGE BOHEMIA - by appointment
address: 1e Great Eastern St, London EC2A 3EJ, UK

reviews.text: We had a great experience at Lounge Bohemia. We had the cocktail tasting menu and the mocktail tasting menu, and both were innovative, creative and tasty! The atmosphere was very chill and cozy. The best part was the service - we had the most attentive waiter who took the time to explain each cocktail, and you could tell they loved what they did. Felt very comfortable the whole time and didn't mind the price after such good treatment! Would recommend!

Very beautiful and intimate place, with great décor. The cocktails were well crafted with good explanations, but I found them a bit expensive. The only downside is that I
could only pay by cash or bank transfer, which was a bit annoying. I’d recommend the place for a date, although I’ve had better cocktails elsewhere (a matter of taste).
I love this place! The drinks are so creative, interactive, and almost whimsical. The service was really friendly and thoughtful too. This is a very fun drinking experience. Can’t wait to go back

Best cocktail bar I've ever been to! Not only was the popcorn the best I've ever tasted in my life, but I love the fact that they continuously top your bowl up with more popcorn a very simple detail but a great addition to the service. SHOW STOPPING COCKTAILS that you could eat !!!! Priced at a reasonable price, considering all you get. A nice relaxed, understated Bohemian vibe, And due to its appointment, only nature, I feel like the relaxed atmosphere had more of a selective crowd inside, wasn't full of influencers on their phones but just people enjoying their drinks

Naturally this is all to do with taste, and in this case it didn't sit well with me, but each to their own. Scandinavian furniture and minor theatrics in serving does not warrant these steep prices, let alone excuse the meagre quality of the booze-soaked confusions that LOUNGE BOHEMIA call cocktails. Considering we were one of two tables in the entire bar, the wait time for my recommended whiskey cocktail had exceeded limits of what can be considered acceptable. Upon being served said (premixed) cocktail from a recessed Bible, I can only surmise that the wait time can be attributed to the host having chiselled the pages from the holy book in that time himself. I'll offer my thanks nevertheless, to hatted host, for helping us guide through the almost abstract menu (albeit patronisingly and in a squatted position before our table). A minor suggestion for easing the hosts' workflow that is already swamped by pompous table-side lectures, would be an attempt to concretise the menu. Enough of the whimsy. That being said, the alcoholic gummies that were served were indeed good, and thankfully didn't come with any speeches or interpretive dances. A final word of advice, it might be best for the hosts/servers to not awkwardly stare down their guests when they walk in, and say nothing. Considering their casual dress and apish squatting, it's hard to tell who is staff and who isn't, and silently gawking at new-comers is hardly welcoming. But if this is all to your taste, no judgement. Enjoy yourself.

We booked dinner at Gaucho for a celebration, and I was genuinely looking forward to it — especially as it was my first visit after many years of living in London. The food itself was good, and I’ve included photos to reflect that. Unfortunately, the service on this particular Wednesday evening didn’t our meet expectations.

We arrived at 6:30pm, and by around 7:30pm the restaurant was full and busy. What stood out was that one waitress appeared to be managing a very large number of tables on her own. She was consistently attentive, taking orders, serving drinks, and clearing plates throughout the evening.

In contrast, the managers on duty seemed less engaged with the wider dining area. Although they occasionally helped clear a table or two, there were several moments when nearby tables needed attention and guests were waiting. At one point, a manager spent considerable time with a group of regular customers but did not check in with surrounding tables, including ours. Eventually, I had to signal to request the bill. It was brought over, but there was no check‑in about how our meal had been or any closing interaction. For a bill of over £220, the lack of acknowledgement felt surprising. Before leaving, we made a point to thank the waitress who had been working so hard, and she responded warmly. However, as we exited, the front‑of‑house team were engaged in conversation and didn’t notice us leaving.

Based on this experience, I don’t plan to return, and I wouldn’t recommend this particular location to family or friends or colleagues. The food was enjoyable, but the service on this visit didn’t reflect the standard I expected. I genuinely hope the team reviews their approach to workload distribution and guest engagement, as the waitress working that evening was doing an excellent job under pressure.

We had a great experience at the restaurant. Jessica was an excellent server — very friendly, attentive, and professional. She helped us choose a bottle of wine, and her recommendation was perfect. The wine was excellent and made our evening even more enjoyable. Thank you, Jessica, for the wonderful service!

Amazing restaurant has the rump steak and prawns for starter was exceptional. Also a special mention to such an amazing waitress Rossella really made our first time here and will be back. Beautiful service and amazing food. Very very happy thanks Gaucho's

For the price point, this was a disappointing experience. On a Friday night, the restaurant felt short-staffed. The food was mediocre: all the steaks were over-seasoned, two arrived cold, and the chips were so salty they were inedible.

The wrong sides were brought to the table, and although staff said they would be removed from the bill, they still appeared at the end. The steak knives were poor quality and struggled to cut through a marinated steak that I should have been able to cut with a butter knife.

Drinks were slow to arrive every time we ordered. Service missed many basics: clearing plates, pouring wine, checking in on the table, and serving in a timely manner. Instead, staff were often seen talking among themselves.

My last visit to this Gaucho was ten years ago. I had hoped for improvement, but it was average then and remains average now. The only positives were the warm greeting on entry,the farewell and cocktails.

I cannot rave enough about this Restaurant & Bar. The staff were welcoming and got all 10 of us sorted with drinks as soon as we arrived. After approx 20 minutes we were shown to our table. Wow, what an amazingly decorated underground restaurant. Our host was Miri, who was fantastic from the first encounter until we all left. Excellent advice on starters and drinks. The starters came very quickly and everyone was impressed with both the quality and the serving size. The wine selection was very special and we choose wonderful Red that complemented the Steak perfectly.
The mains & sides were brought out and everyone was blown away by the quality of the food. The chips were really good, spinach was outrageously good and the tender stem broccoli was the same. The 400g Ribeye was one of the best Steaks I have ever had. I had the cheesecake (as suggested by Miri) & I was done. The whole experience from start to end was amazing.

name: Gaucho City of London
address: 1 Bell Inn Yard, London EC3V 0BL, UK

reviews.text:
Recently visited Gaucho City and overall had a very enjoyable experience. The restaurant has a stylish, lively atmosphere that works well for both business dinners and special occasions. The steak was cooked well and full of flavour, and the sides complemented the meal nicely.
Service was friendly and attentive, although there were moments when it felt slightly rushed. Prices are on the higher side, but the quality of the food and the setting largely justify it. A solid choice if you’re looking for a premium steakhouse in the City.

A paradise for meat lovers, serving up rich South American flavours that make every steak feel like it flew in first class. The cuts are tender, the chimichurri is addictive, and the wine selection is so good you’ll start feeling like a connoisseur even if you’re not. Stylish, bold, and dangerously delicious. 🥩🍷🔥

Ambience was absolutely lovely, service was top quality except for the gentleman on the entrance (bold headed in a tux like suit) who was quite rude because we had a hidden disability and had to use the lift. Dog friendly which is amazing, and the steak and shrimps were to die for
The food was great. I had the ribeye and my partner the fish. The atmosphere is great. The service is on top with competent and friendly staff.

We had a fantastic evening at Gaucho City. Shared a 700g Chateaubriand with my colleague, cooked perfectly medium rare and absolutely delicious. Starters and sides were excellent, and the staff were wonderfully attentive.

We came in to experience the set menu from a Virgin Experience Days voucher.
The staff were wonderful and accommodating, and very friendly. As expected for such a high-end restaurant, everything was top notch.
The restaurant was classically decorated, low-lit and felt very intimate, which is what we had hoped for.
The food itself was DELICIOUS. We enjoyed almost all of the dishes, but some were not to our taste. A fan favourite was the beef bourguignon and the chocolate mousse. The beetroot salad was the least favourite, and felt it was too niche a dish to not be able to swap out.
Aside from this, we would definitely return, but would order from the A La Carte menu, not a set menu.

5/5 would recommend

I came here with 3 other people tonight and we had a great evening. All in all, the food was delicious, the service was friendly and the ambience was lovely.

We came for the 6 course and cocktail menu, I had a pornstar mocktail which was refreshing and tasty. We had beetroot with goats cheese and walnut, and salmon with crème fraiche as an aperitif. I then had ham hock pate with coleslaw which both complemented each other very well.

For the main I had beef bourguignon with mashed potato, I also had a honey and mustard salad which did not have much honey or mustard flavour, but it was still good nonetheless. The beef itself was exquisite, it really melted in the mouth and I’d definitely recommend.

For dessert I had a chocolate mousse which was rich and very tasty. There were also scotch wafers with cream inside which were very crunchy. I then had a cup of tea to finish.

I did notice a lot of cutlery being dropped, the restaurant is big so it was rather noisy, and I noticed quite a few back of house staff walking through the restaurant area. These and the salad feedback are the main constructive points I’d raise. The staff were very friendly and the kitchen was accommodating of food preferences and menu changes.

Overall, everything was lovely, an evening to remember for sure :)

We visited for lunch and had the 5 course taster menu. The staff were impeccable from start to finish - friendly, welcoming and professional. We loved the seating and design of the restaurant; just the right amount of space between tables so you didn't feel on top of the people near to you. Acoustics were also great as I could hear my partner and not everyone else.

The pace of the meal was perfect. We did not feel rushed and food arrived promptly for the start courses but then there were slightly bigger gaps between the following courses. It was very impressive indeed.

The food - each course was as expected for a restaurant of this standard - excellent and faultless. We loved everything served and would definitely return for another meal.

We had been gifted a 6 course menu here with a cocktail.

When we arrived we were asked to wait at the bar which was ridiculously crowded, there were over 20 people here and only 6 stools and no hangers left for our coats.

We were taken to our table and everyone from there was attentive and friendly.

1st was a choice of cocktail.

2nd and 3rd course was a few slices of beetroot and a little pancake with some salmon on.

4th was an option of makeral pate and ham hock? There was an option to upgrade £3 to have bone marrow salad. We had the makeral which was nice and very fresh and the Bone marrow which was very small but tasty.

5th course was the main, which was steak and a choice of sauce. I asked for my steak rare and was recommended to go medium rare, which I did, it arrived closer to well done.  We added fries (£12) and creamed spinach (£8.5)

Dessert was yummy we had chocolate mouse and lemon posset(this was the best one). Then tea and coffee to finish.

On top of our voucher it cost us £60 with service(we also had one drink each at the bar while we wait).

Was a nice experience as a gift but I wouldn’t go back.

I was a little apprehensive after reading some of the previous reviews, but our experience here was absolutely wonderful.

This visit was a gift through a Virgin Experience Voucher, and we were genuinely impressed from start to finish.

We chose the three-course meal with a cocktail each and couldn’t resist adding a few extras.

The food was delicious especially the sticky toffee pudding which I’m still thinking about.

The service was also friendly and attentive, even with how busy it was.

Thank you to the team at London Steakhouse for a truly memorable evening!

Haven't been to this place in years. But visited today with some family friends. We are Vietnamese and this is certainly a more high end establishment. This is reflected in the price being slightly higher than your typical Vietnamese restaurants but the quality and quantity of the food is certainly higher also. I was pleasantly surprised on my return and had a most enjoyable meal. We had the banh cuon, banh uot, goi, cha gio, bun bo hue, bun cha hanoi, and com ga. All items were excellent and very authentic. To top it all off, after discussing among ourselves how delicious the chili sauce is, we ended up having a lovely nice chat with the manager too.

The food at Viet Grill was excellent. We shared a mix of meat, fish, and vegetarian starters, all of which were delicious. The bone marrow pho was unlike any pho I have had before and very tasty. There was also a good range of non-alcoholic drink options. I especially enjoyed the sour plum tonic, unusual flavours but really enjoyable.

Service was a bit mixed. Our mains took quite a while to arrive, and one member of staff came across as slightly surly, though others were friendly and helpful. The music was also far too loud for my liking.

Viet Grill is the favourite spot on the Kingsland Road strip of a Vietnamese girlfriend of mine.  I like the food but my enthusiasm is dimmed by the fact that it is 30% to 40% more expensive than their competitors on Kingsland Road.  The extra dosh does buy you a nice decor, and romantic dim lighting.  Somewhere you could take a date.  Unlike their competitors that mostly offer a canteen atmosphere.

Our server advised us well on how much to order for a non ravenous table of 5.  From the starters section we had Hanoi style Banh Cuon, fish sauce caramel chicken wings,  grilled aubergine with minced pork, salt and pepper squid.  All were good.  The salt and pepper squid was served a little differently than in other restaurants on the strip, in that squid was first deep fried and then stir fried with some onion and peppers.  Banh cuon is served by some other restaurants nearby, but not all.  It is similar to Chinese cheun fun.  Viet Grill offer three regional variations of this less commonly available dish.

From the mains we had the sizzling mixed seafood stir fry, which was the only disappointing dish, being characterless and a little bland.   Stir fried morning glory was dependable if unremarkable.  Beef stew redolent with cinnamon and lemongrass was tender and delicious.  The best of our mains was the claypot catfish, stewed in the same fish sauce caramel that coated the chicken wing starter.  This is a somewhat uncommon dish not available in every Kingsland Rd restaurant. We needed three servings of plain rice for the 5 of us.

I did like the food but questioned the pricing compared to nearby competitors.   That said, the decor and atmosphere is much better than the other Kingsland Rd restaurants.  I would recommend Viet Grill for a romantic date, or when taking out an elderly relative who is put off by the basic canteen-like atmosphere of most of the other Vietnamese offerings on Kingsland Road.

Looking for value for money come here.
We had a group of 10 and had the set meal 2 which worked out £22 a head. Free to bring in outside drinks too. Unreal and left feeling very full
Fantastic experience and there are some fun unique dishes offered here that we recommend you try, especially the rice paper crepes!

Incredible experience from the moment I booked the space for my Galentine's event up until the moment we packed up to leave. Alex is so accommodating and the staff for the event (Jordan and Molly) were such a delight! The guests loved the space and I would absolutely return for a future event.

I visited this site for the first time to meet a friend and I was amazed at how friendly the staff were and especially considering it was a busy Friday night, the service was also excellent. Our food arrived quite quickly and was piping hot and tasted great. I really enjoyed the atmosphere at this location, you could see why it was so busy as it is such a nice location. Loved the decor, loved the different sections of the pub as well as we had a table booked in a little nook which gave us privacy and we didn't need to shout across the table. Fully recommend.

A busy London vibing pub opposite Liverpool Station, a trendy place to hangout for a quick drink,  lounges on different levels and a private one to rent on the top floor.  A great selection of beers available on the tap. Delicious smelling food you'll not be disappointed. It also hosts a nice outdoor drinking area with tables and chairs for when the weather's good

Great pub - check out the upstairs area! Dart boards and a great place to watch the match !

You can also order from your phone and have everything delivered directly to your table! Great staff - highly recommend

I had an excellent experience booking “The office bar” in the first floor. The staff were really friendly the booking process was seamless and we were allowed to play music in the sound system and dance. I couldn’t recommend more for a private function. Very reasonably priced. A big thank you !

We visited Poppies Fish & Chips and had a fantastic experience. There was a wide variety of fresh fish options, and everything we tried was absolutely delicious. The quality and flavour were truly impressive.

A special thank you to Funda Hanım for her warm hospitality and friendly attitude. She made us feel very welcome and gave us excellent recommendations, which made our visit even more enjoyable.

We were very pleased with the whole experience and will definitely be coming back. Highly recommended!

Perfect fish - my haddock was fresh, succulent, crisp batter, just the right thickness. The chips are good (not the best I’ve had), tea is hot, coke is cold, mushy peas the way it should be. Forget the curry sauce though, it’s lumpy and pretty tasteless.

Service was great. We went on a Saturday afternoon and seating was fast.

Easily the best fish and chips I’ve ever had, and it’s clear why they’ve been in business for so long. I also tried some dishes that are less popular with tourists: whitebait (similar to French fries, but made with tiny whole white fish) and cod roe (battered and deep-fried caviar). Both were something completely new to me and absolutely delicious.

Less than 10 minutes walk from Liverpool Street, Poppies manages to be both a decent counter chippy and a full table service restaurant, and it does both well.

Visited a couple of times over the years. This visit as a group of three, seated for table service. Calamari and chips for me this time, crisp coating and tender inside. A decent wedge of lemon. Baked beans and mushy peas for the table. Chips thick cut and fluffy within. Batter light and golden. Everything tasted clean from the fryer. Portions filling.

Nice cutlery and colourful plates added to our experience. And it’s not every chipper that will serve up a G&T and a glass of wine, alongside.

All in all, good chippy, quality ingredients, quick service, a bit pricey but this is in Shoreditch.

(Last visit May 2016)

This establishment lives up to its reputation as being a great fish and chip shop. We arrived on a Friday evening and were delighted they could accommodate a table for 4 for us. Food was excellent but the portions are a bit on the smaller side. They could have added a few more chips and more tartare sauce. Food was well cooked and not greasy at all. The service was quick, efficient and friendly
Great food, historical settings, excellent service.  will make it a point to eat there if I'm back in town.

Very nice steak. Had rump, not the most expensive cut, but it was done very well. Seasoning was on point, chips were great, beer was nice and the atmosphere at lunch (2 pm ) was pretty solid. Great waiter. Dunno, pretty perfect really. Only downside was that although the benches look the part, ultimately they weren't very comfortable. Top marks though.

A very tasty portion of pie and mash in an entirely unpretentious manner.
Not cheap but very good.

Very much a meat eater's paradise but then that's how they set out their stall so you can't complain at the lack of vegetarian options. Several excellent specials on the board today but get in early or they soon disappear. Desserts are very much of the school dinners type enjoyed by City gents. Prices are very reasonable for the location and associated clientele though vegetables tend to be extra unless a key part of the dish. Serving staff both friendly and entertaining.

The worst and most expensive roast beef dinner I have had, tough elastic beef, sloppy watery spinach, and god knows what they did to the roast poatoes, black brown and texture of boiled potatoes, a pint of flat warm lemonade from a big plastic bottle, the waitress kept repeating with a scowl that service was not included, I went with a friend after listening to someone famous reminisce about his childhood memories of this place, I understand that it is smack bang in the City of London and assumed that they did not like our appearance and thus the hostile reception and the terrible food. Will never return.
This review was for my experience of this joint before it's closure, my original review at the time was not published by google for some reason.

We visited the restaurant on a Sunday afternoon.
We were welcomed and seated by a lovely lady.
The restaurant wasn’t busy at all time we got there.
We ordered a sharing platter which was a great idea as we got to try few things instead of ordering one side.
For the mains we had tofu pad Thai and chicken pad Thai.
Both were very delicious, full of flavour.
My partner who usually doesn’t eat Asian food and is not a big foodie really liked it so it must have been good.
My tofu one was great too and the portion size was generous.
The prices are very reasonable too.
We both had drinks, I had a Thai tea with condensed milk.
The service was very nice especially the lady with a pony tail who welcomed us and a guy who came later. He was very friendly, polite and helpful. He looked after the customers and made sure everyone is happy, they deserve a recognition.
I can recommend this place.
Thank You!

Delicious! We went for dinner with some friends, and it was easily some of the best Thai food I’ve ever had. The fried calamari were outstanding, and my Pad Thai was absolutely delicious. Just a heads-up—the green curry was a bit on the spicy side for some in our group, so be prepared for a kick! 🌶️🍚 I would highly recommend this place to anyone craving authentic Thai cuisine.

Overall I’ve given it 4 stars but it’s more like 4.5. The food was lovely I got the flat noodles with chicken and a lemon ice tea no milk. The ice tea was a little bitter for my liking but it went quite well with the noodles as they were on the sweeter side. And the chicken was a tad bit dry but otherwise the meal was good. The atmosphere was actually lovely very warm, artsy feel and good music, the only thing was the seating wasn’t very comfortable. It’s good for a quick meal so I would probably go back for lunch again as overall it was a pleasant experience.
I tried the Pad Kra Prow and Thai milk tea — both were amazing! The stir-fry had the perfect balance of spice and basil, and the milk tea was creamy and refreshing. Highly recommend!
Amazing food! We took a second portion because it was too good! Atmosphere very friendly! They even speak italian (like me)! Grazie! Everything delicious ♥️

Quiet when we came in but it very quickly got busy so would recommend booking. All staff were friendly and attentive. Would recommend and we would come back.
We had a lovely experience with Mack. The food was outstanding. The atmosphere was relaxed and comfortable. As an international guest - I highly recommend.

Our server Mandy was fantastic, he gave delish recommendations and we had a wonderful meal. Service was amazing, very relaxing feel. The chickpeas with spinach were a surprising standout. Lamb balti was delish. BYOB is always a plus. Thoroughly recommend
Amazing meal and service! Our waiter Tanmay was very attentive, helpful and friendly. Also they have a separate menu for vegans. Would whole heartedly recommend

Not often I rate a curry house 5★, but this place delivers some of the best curry you’ll find. The menu is extensive and they’re more than happy to cater to individual tastes.

For starters, I had the sheesh kebab, well spiced and full of flavour. For the main, I ordered the garlic chicken masala and asked for it hotter than usual; it was phenomenal. My friend ordered the chicken dopiaza, which was also top quality.

The Peshawari and garlic naans were excellent sides, and our server Farhan was attentive and friendly throughout.

The only reason for 3★ on the atmosphere was that we arrived while there was a very large, lively table in, which made conversation at our table a bit difficult — nothing negative about the venue itself.

Overall, if you’re looking for a proper curry in London, look no further.
