reviews.text:
Had a really great time at Balls Brothers Austin Friars. Everything just worked, good vibes, great food and a relaxed but polished atmosphere that makes you want to stay longer than planned.

Big shout-out to the manager Alberto, who honestly made the experience even better. Super attentive, really knowledgeable and genuinely professional without ever feeling stiff or overbearing. He checked in at just the right moments, gave great recommendations and made us feel properly looked after.

If you’re looking for a solid spot in the City with great service and a welcoming feel, this place is a winner. Will definitely be back! 🍷👏

We hosted our work Christmas party for a group of 126 people, and it was absolutely fantastic! From the very beginning, the communication with the team was excellent—every detail was handled smoothly and efficiently.

The staff on the night were super helpful and incredibly friendly, making sure everyone felt welcome and taken care of. The three-course meal was delicious, with plenty of compliments from our team about the quality of the food.

They were also extremely accommodating when our live band arrived to set up. The space worked perfectly for both the seated dinner and the band’s performance, creating a great atmosphere for the evening.

I can’t recommend Austin Friars Balls Brothers enough for any large event or party. A huge thank you to the team for helping us create such a memorable night!

Incredible. Had my hen party here and it was so good. The food isn’t what you go there for so I get it’s not the best quality. But the vibes, fun and party make up for it! So so good highly recommend for fun with your besties!!

Great pub, serving great food with a great service.

The venue looked fantastic and I was hosted my Flo and Alberto who looked after us with a great service, constantly smiling and making sure we had a wonderful time. Food was also incredible. Thank you to the whole team.
Great pub! Flo did a great job to bring the place back to life with a strong team. I have been there a couple of times for different occasions and I will def be back!

Hands down the greatest pub experience in LDN (and beyond). I want you to imagine the greatest conceivable buzz with the tastiest sandwiches and Portuguese plates you’ve ever had. To share with your friends. I cannot believe how good The Macbeth is — this is everything I want from a Saturday evening!

The Prego and Bifana sandwiches are famed for a reason and do not disappoint. We also shared the pink firs in aioli, fried mussels, Peri chicken and lamb Vindaloo. All ridiculously good. The Macbeth delivers both a fantastic vibe and out-of-this-world food; I am so excited to come back and explore the menu again, which changes daily. Unbelievable spot. 10/10!!

Had a really really good Sunday lunch here. Bit noisy at the front of the pub but we got seated near the kitchen area and it was quieter. The food was great, lovely staff and a nice carafe of house red  🍷 … sadly they had run out of a few things by 4.30 but we got almost everything we wanted… ( no cheesy leeks !) 10/10

If you are after Portuguese style cuisine and a good wine and beer selection then this is the place to go. Our favorite was the bifana   sandwich and the salted cod served on shoe string fries with soft boiled egg, honestly can’t wait to go back. The orange wine also paired nicely with the mussels and we had the flan for desert.
Unreal food and service. The New Years set menu was one of our favourite dining experiences of the year. Stoked this is our local in the heart of Hoxton!

Went with a friend for their opening night. There was an excited buzz in the place and a touch of nervousness to get everything right. They did. In spades. The atmosphere of the original has been kept but the food coming out the kitchen is a wonderful trip to Portugal. Small plates, incredible Bifana (MUST ORDER) and delicious seafood were finished off by a perfect slice of flan. Go now before they are too busy to get a booking at.

Went to see Lizzie Esau live. It's a little hard to find at first. Plenty of space both inside and outside. Prices were reasonable for drinks. Easy access to the bars and the performance space. Sound quality was good and as it's a small venue, a good view is fairly ready to find. Would definitely go again. Only downside for me was that to get back to Paddington afterwards isn't the easiest of trips.

I enjoyed seeing Mint Field and a little bit of Avishag Cohen Rodrigues here last Sunday. It's worth knowing that there's no cloakroom at the venue (it is only a bar after all), but the helpful staff managed to look after my coat and backpack between them during the gig, which was very much appreciated. Would happily come here again.

Great bar with live music room and a huge outdoor patio. I used to come here 15 years ago and it has not lost its character. Not sure about the service as they didn't acknowledge me for a while so I decide to check out live music without the drink and then left.

The food is tasty, the service is fair enough. On the weekends it is very very crowded and loud so the staff is doing their best to manage that crowd. I do definitely recommend to book if you are a larger group. The garden ares is such lovely with all the lights and if you book in advance you can get a table under the tent where you can stay safe in the rain

Great pub with outside space. Ideally have a reservation on saturdays to make sure you get inside but usually its not too crowded on saturdays. They have a really good cider on tap (my fav) not too sweet, not too dry. They also have food but not really gf options as far as I remember besides crisps. They have loads of outside space and heaters too! They also have three bars - one outside and two inside - top and bottom!

What an experience. We went there for a taster menu and it was good. When I say good, I mean Really GOOD!
I was sceptical about portion sizes at first, however, they proved me wrong - portion sizes were just right and the main thing is - It was mouth watering.
The staff was very attentive, polite and friendly. The atmosphere was calm, with gentle music in the background and dimmed lights.
Would definitely repeat the whole experience.
Recommended.

First visit for a company due and we had a beautiful experience at this venue in December 24. It was booked it for my colleagues many times before and every time I received exceptional feedback. The booking process and customer service were always flawless,  so I already had a positive impression that it would not disappoint the expectations. And in fact,  the venue is very beautiful,  with wonderful decor, great art pieces, and a warm atmosphere. Everything is super cozy. Furthermore, the food was delicious, and the wine choice was just great!  The only thing the lift 🛗 is slow and we stuck on the way down. Looking forward to my next visit here!!
I recommend

Lovely private member’s club in Moorgate. Beautiful decor, traditional, corporate vibe. Has a beautiful roof terrace. Also has a gym and restaurant. Gym seems well equipped, small steam room and they run boxing classes etc there.

Decidedly average tasting menu, everything was well presented but not exciting or interesting. Not a single worthy dish. Service was quite slow and even with a Groupon voucher it wasn't worth the price. Overall pretty subpar. Wouldn't possibly ever want to go again.

I cannot recommend Eight Club Moorgate highly enough, and I especially want to recognise Esther from the team for her outstanding service. From the moment I reached out early in the morning with last-minute requests for breakfast and lunch arrangements, Esther handled everything flawlessly and with a smile. She delivered on the spot, ensuring our meeting ran smoothly and our guests were completely comfortable.

My partners were 100% happy with the experience, and that was entirely down to Esther’s professionalism, efficiency, and genuine care. She went above and beyond, and I honestly can’t thank her enough. If you’re planning an event or meeting at Eight Club, you’ll be in excellent hands with Esther. She is a true credit to the club!

name: The Star of Bethnal Green
address: 359 Bethnal Grn Rd, London E2 6LG, UK

reviews.text:
I celebrated my birthday in the karaoke which was half price because it's January. We were 20 people vibing, it was great to find music in Spanish as well, which is not the norm. The staff helped me with napkins, lighter, and knife for my cake.
Pizza was very good, non alcoholic options available, decent prices for all.
After karaoke was over, we went downstairs and had the best time with the best DJ in London. He really read the room and played absolute BANGERS.

100% will be back!

So arrived here last night around 11pm. 2 door staff just standing to the side of the entrance. I proceeded to walk in and then was summoned back outside. I said 'is there a problem?' The lady door person said 'well I am just seeing how much you've had to drink...'. I said 'well clearly not enough,  otherwise I wouldn't be here' (jovial of course). She said 'well I am just looking at the confidence, the way you walked in, you have too much confidence'. I said ' well I think at the age of 49 I should have plenty of confidence by now'. She said 'no sorry not tonight' meaning I wasn't be allowed entry. I said ' OK fine' and walked to another pub. I had already had a drink, but was clearly NOT drunk. I am not a child, I am almost 50 years if age, with my best mate who is 55. We are not kids out for a fight, just an honest drink. Is it your door policy to ask people to get down on their knees and beg to get in, rather than walk straight in the door of the pub, with 'confidence ' like you would expect your customers to have? After all the door staff were not blocking the door vetting people, they were merely standing by the side of thw door allowed people to walk in unchallenged. A very bizarre reaction from your doorstaff and certainly not warranted,  especially considering that it is Christmas party time.

Lovely night for the battle of the brewery event. The general service by Dasian on the bar was brilliant and the Manager , Archie was great when dealing with the tasters from each brewer too. Overall a very enjoyable night and full of great drinks and vibes all around

A good East London boozer with warm and friendly staff, and some great burgers.
A good choice of beers, including local craft breweries. I did not stay for any events, but I bet it is.lots of fun in the evenings.
For me it was a nice quiet spot for a drink on a Saturday lunchtime, away for the bustle of Bethnal Green Road

George and DeShaun were on the bar on a Monday night and they were lovely. Never been to the bar before but they had that je ne sais quoi that means I will bring my work team here at every opportunity. What a lovely duo.

name: The Crown and Shuttle
address: 226 Shoreditch High St, London E1 6PJ, UK

reviews.text: It’s a pub so my friend suggested there because she likes beer. It offers a good selection of beers. I am not the beer person but she likes it! It is at a very central location in Shoteditch High Street and so packed on weekends. I went there on a Saturday evening and it was so crowded. The atmosphere is nice, mostly young people’s destionation and staff is nice. You cannot really talk and hear each other if you want a chilled evening but I suggest for a pub experience!

I hired the upstairs private venue for my 30th birthday party and it was absolutely perfect! The staff and manager were super helpful in answering my questions, hosting and cleaning up after the party. Guests said the food was of high quality and absolutely delicious too! Would definitely recommend hiring the venue for a party!! The only minus was that there was no sound coming from the TV though it had worked previously, and we briefly had some issues with the sound system but that was fixed soon after. Thanks for making it a great party!

Bit of an odd introduction to the pub at 6pm on a Tuesday when we were asked by the bouncer to open our bags to prove we weren’t smuggling alcohol into the pub (not something men in their 40’s typically do on a Tuesday after work). But once inside it’s quite a decent pub, nice atmosphere, and a good outdoor area at the back.

Must be the only pub in London that is NOT DOG FRIENDLY. Which has changed recently, staff are also oddly blunt and unhelpful and perform bag checks upon entry… yes for a pub.

I was told ‘it’s too busy’ for dogs, when clearly not. (My dog is also a miniature breed). I was also told “it’s illegal to have dogs in a pub as they don’t have insurance” - ridiculous.

Used to be a good spot, seems like the place think a bit too much of themselves now.

Ended up in a ‘bar’ the other side of the road and they were completely welcoming. No longer good place for a drink, go elsewhere there’s plenty of good options nearby.

We were in the private function room and Juliette was behind the bar - she was so lovely and her service was perfect. She advised us on which burger to order and we had a lovely chat! Would definitely recommend for anyone having a function.

Beautifully decorated with a sleek, modern design and a clean, open view of the bar area. The service was attentive and friendly, which made the experience pleasant. We tried a few starters, honestly, they were underwhelming, so I’d suggest going for the larger plates, which might be their stronger point. Prices are reasonable for the setting, and overall it’s worth a visit.

The Anthologist is one of those rare places that strikes the perfect balance between atmosphere, flavor, and hospitality. From the moment you walk in, you’re welcomed by a warm, stylish setting that feels both relaxed and refined — the kind of place that works equally well for a casual lunch, after-work drinks, or a special dinner.

The menu is creative without being pretentious. Every dish feels thoughtfully crafted — fresh ingredients, bold flavors, and beautiful presentation. The small plates are ideal for sharing (the [insert a dish you liked, e.g., Korean-fried cauliflower or truffle mac & cheese] was a standout), and the cocktails are exceptional — well-balanced, inventive, and beautifully served.

Service is another strong point. The staff are friendly, attentive, and genuinely passionate about what they do. They’re always happy to offer recommendations, which makes the experience feel personal rather than formulaic.

Whether you’re there for brunch, cocktails, or dinner, The Anthologist delivers every time. It’s stylish but not stuffy, vibrant but comfortable — a perfect spot to unwind and enjoy great food and good company.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ Highly recommended.

Utter abomination of a meal. For £56!!! They’re laughing at us. Beetroot smoked salmon? Two wisps of it, only really detected with a magnifying glass. Crayfish salad? Invisible sea-monkeys more like. Ok soggy bread to boot.’and how about ice cold roast turkey with a shivering no-bacon pig in blanket, and gravy as watery as water. Under-cooked parsnips. The cheesecake was kind of ok. Music so loud you can’t hear the person next to you shout and service so slow our first drinks arrived way after the first course had been served. Utterly shocking. This place should be ashamed of themselves.

Excellent venue with a great vibe. I met a friend here for midweek drinks and small plates, and it did not disappoint. The atmosphere was lively, the service attentive, and we even received a great wine recommendation.

The food was outstanding, and we’ll definitely be returning. I love the bar and dining area, and even the toilets were impressive! The décor and lighting throughout are beautiful, making it a perfect spot for a date night too.

We had a dinner and a group get together after that with around 50 people. We enjoyed the food. I forgot her name but a Romanian waiter helped to our table, she is very friendly and attentive.
I also liked the decor, it was very on point with the holiday season.

name: So Japanese Private Dining
address: So Japanese, 5 Middlesex St, London E1 7AA, UK

reviews.text: A rare taste of Japan in London, paired with that hard-to-find Japanese warmth and hospitality. The perfectly grilled unagi don—every bite reminded me of Kyoto: sweet, smoky, melt-in-the-mouth goodness. The photos speak for themselves. Thank you, So, for such a delicious weekend 🍱🤍

One of the best meals I’ve eaten! I ordered cod and it was divine!😍 Definitely will come back. Also, great staff and atmosphere. If you want a calm, relaxing evening with a very tasty food you should definitely visit this place.

For my birthday, I decided to try Japanese cuisine for the very first time in a non-westernised, non-commercialised restaurant in which a true taste of Japan could be properly experienced. Their menu was limited but with good reason as they perfected what they served, embodying the phrase ‘less is more.’ I am beyond happy to say that the So restaurant in London delivered every part of my culinary desires combined with friendly and attentive customer service!

Upon arrival with my dad and brother, we were welcomed with all the kind hospitality needed to warm us up on a chilly autumn’s evening. The staff were few but exceptionally gifted in their dedication to every customer, always smiling and happy to serve, creating a tranquil atmosphere that put us at ease immediately. They were very understanding of our lack of experience with Japanese cuisine and patiently explained their menu to us in detail. I was deeply interested in their Unagi Kabayaki (grilled eel with a sweet savoury glaze) ever since I saw it in a food show based in Japan. I never thought you could find such a specialty dish in England and was drawn to the So restaurant for this specific reason. They served it to me in an Una Ju form (grilled eel served on top of rice in a rice box) and it did not disappoint! The texture of the rice was fluffy and creamy, combining with the flavours of the grilled eel perfectly. It was cooked beautifully with a slightly charred skin concealing within a white, buttery meat that melted in my mouth. I highly recommend this dish to anyone visiting. We also tried the sushi (Nigiri), including the bluefin tuna, yellowtail, and salmon, all of which were clean tasting and rich in texture. The bluefin tuna and salmon were the highlights for me. Finally, we finished the meal with an assortment of desserts, including the matcha chocolate cake and hojicha terrine, delightfully recommended to us by the lovely lady serving us. She surprised me with a happy birthday message and song along with all the other staff! They also generously blessed us with one dessert and some genmaicha (roasted brown rice green tea) on the house as a most welcome surprise.

I was truly comforted and satisfied by the end of my visit and can honestly say that coming to the So restaurant was the highlight of my birthday. It was worth every penny spent! My only regret is that I did not get to thank the lovely lady who served us with such heartfelt warmth for the incredible meal - If you’re reading this, thank you so much for making my birthday an extra special one! Your kindness completed our experience with you. After all, what is a beautifully crafted meal if not united with all the warmth and hospitality you showed toward us on such a special day?

I will definitely be visiting again in the near future.

The best Japanese meal I have ever eaten!
The food was absolutely delicious and so carefully prepared. The staff were so welcoming and lovely. I can’t recommend this beautiful restaurant enough! Will definitely be back :)

The best Unagi rice that I have had in London 😋highly recommended👍🏻will come back for that again.

Hojicha Terrine is also very yummy, good for 2 people to share.

Dashimaki ommelette was a bit different from the one that I tried in Japan, the taste is not bad.

Good environment and nice staff, have a great time there.

The Pho was absolutely amazing!! 😍🍜

I brought a friend to Song Que Cafe as he was preparing for a trip to Vietnam and wanted a taste of the cuisine beforehand, and this spot definitely delivered.

We ordered a great spread: the pho with combo beef (rare steak, flank, tendon, tripe) was easily the highlight, deep, rich broth with beautifully balanced flavours that felt authentic and comforting. The banh xeo (crispy pancake with prawns and chicken) was golden, light, and packed with flavour, pairing well with the fresh herbs and dipping sauce. We also had the mì xao bo (beef stir-fried noodles), which were well-seasoned and satisfying, and the gà nướng (lemongrass chicken), which was juicy, aromatic, and perfectly cooked.

The vibe inside was busy but relaxed, and the service was fast and friendly. Food arrived quickly, and the staff were attentive throughout.

The only slightly awkward part was at the entrance, each time we entered, we were asked where we were going. Not sure if it was for security or just routine, but it felt a bit overbearing, especially when I had to pop out briefly to move the car and was questioned again right after needing to attend a phonecall.

Still, the food speaks for itself. If you're after bold, classic Vietnamese flavours in London, Song Que remains one of the best spots.

Went there early on a Saturday just as they opened and the place filled up quickly. Certainly is a popular place based on its deserved reputation for good quality Vietnamese fare. Portions are generous and food is quite possibly the best of its kind in London. A must-have is the beef pho with all the different cuts (even the tripe). My partner had the spicy bun noodles and it was perfectly spicy and a little sour (just as it should be). Our waiter was friendly and efficient. Chap who initially showed us in wasn’t so…

The food is very good and we didn’t have to wait long. In my personal taste, the Stewed Caramelised Fish was a little salty but everything else was delicious. The iced coffee was also good. The staff were friendly and service was excellent. It’s a place I will definitely come back. I had a great Vietnamese meal today.

This Bun Thit Nuong is such a refreshing bowl of delicate noodles and perfectly grilled pork. The chargrilled pork is very tasty,  tender and savoury… I can say delicious and delicious in every mouthful…I love pickled vegetables and their nuoc cham. Service is super friendly and helpful. This is probably the best Vietnamese on Kingsland..

The service is good. We were sat on the same table as these two ladies who were very loud though which made it hard to enjoy our experience here. Waiters were super nice and food didn’t take too long. Had the pho with chicken and beef - it was lacking in flavour, chicken and meat had no taste also quite dry … even with the addition of sriracha it just felt like a bowl of hot water with noodles; as opposed to a flavourful warm broth . Tried the spring rolls which were crunchy and very tasty, ordered more but the second batch was oilier than expected. Everything on the menu does look tasty, would probably not get the pho again though. Pho - £16
Spring rolls - £8

Went there as a large group for a mates birthday. The food was amazing but the service was slow and some of the dishes took ages to come out. Maybe it was just a busy night! Would go there again one day. Cheers

I came here by chance, feeling absolutely exhausted after a long day... I ordered the Pho soup and jasmine tea – and it was exactly what I needed! The soup was full of flavor, warm and comforting, with lots of fresh herbs and greens – it truly lifted me up 💛 I also had a juicy, fresh orange for a refreshing finish – just perfect.

It's a very cozy place with a super friendly staff – I felt really welcomed and taken care of.
I highly recommend this spot – the food, atmosphere, and service were all amazing. I’ll definitely be coming back! 😊

i sat down at mien tay expecting great food and those expectations were still surpassed. me and my dad came in here starving and i haven't needed to eat for two days - it is very filling, the portion sizes are of incredible value.. you have been warned! the service was..how to say.. Minimal.... by which i mean very straight to the point, you're here for a delicious meal not for small talk with your waiter. had to call staff over rather than them coming to us but we didn't mind. starters were as good as we had heard, my dish (ginger duck + rice) was wonderful, flavourful, and hearty. it seems there is a lot of love going into this cooking.

This is your spot for great authentic Vietnamese food. The food is really amazing and most of the visitors are asian what for me is a great sign. The place isn't the most romantic but if you want to impress with food give this a go.

Real disappointment.

We have been coming here for years and came here to eat on a Sunday.

The Banh Xeo was stale and tasteless - like it had been prepared the day before and filling microwaved.

The other meals (chow mein, curry, and something else unmemorable) were also not great.. bad flavours, not fresh... especially considering how much time it took to have everything served.

Parts of the meal were forgotten and plenty of items were not available. 😕

Service was so so so much worse than anything we'd previously had here... this used to be 5 stars but if I could give 0 this time, I would.

I didn't mind paying the prices previously as the food used to be worth it.. now, it's really not worth the price tag.

Casual, lots of seating, fast service and decent food. We’ve eaten here twice this weekend for breakfast. Sunday was definitely busier than Saturday but there was still plenty of seating. No need to book, but it’s noisy. There is also outdoor seating. Family friendly the menu suits most people and there’s vegetation options. Shubui tea is great quality as was the coffee.

been here a few times and always impressed with the quality of the food/drinks. came here for a set menu christmas dinner with work and everyone really enjoyed themselves, portions were massive and definitely worth the set price.

a very large space with plenty of seating and a nicer area with sofas as well, always friendly service
What a fabulous place. Been meaning to visit for a while and finally had the chance to today. Was not disappointed. Fab aesthetic, great food and amazing staff. Will definitely be back.

A must-visit for motorbike enthusiasts! We finally made it there and were absolutely thrilled. The restaurant was great, the service very polite and friendly, and the atmosphere simply lovely. Awesome shop and, of course, the highlight was the bikes ;)

Part motorcycle clubhouse, part restaurant, and fully “moto culture,” Bike Shed Moto Co. nails the hangout vibe without skimping on the food. I came for the bikes and stayed for the steak—cooked properly, well-seasoned, and genuinely satisfying, not just an afterthought to the décor. The space is lined with beautiful machines and feels purpose-built for meets and ride-outs; even if you don’t ride, you get the atmosphere straight away. Service is relaxed but attentive, the soundtrack fits, and the room hums without being too loud for a proper conversation.

Expect a crowd on weekends and evenings; arriving early or booking ahead is wise. It’s an easy walk from Old Street, and there’s plenty to keep you lingering—bikes to admire, good coffee at the bar, and a menu that goes beyond pub standards. Prices are what you’d expect for central London and the concept, but the quality and setting make it feel worth it. A strong recommendation whether you’re a rider looking for a friendly base or just want a solid meal in a venue with serious character.

🚇Old Street
🍺 £6.80 Level Head

The Windmill is located on a quiet side street just off City Road in Shoreditch, East London. The nearest Tube is Old Street.

Originally built in the late 1800s, the pub you see today was constructed in 1869. The pub has recently undergone significant restoration and renovation, completed in 2022.

This is a good-sized, traditional one-bar pub with a few modern touches. The servery is horseshoe-shaped and centrally located, with the bar area wrapping around it. To the right of the bar is an open kitchen.

The decor consists of a boarded floor, a mix of seating, green wall panelling, and some vintage signage, but my favourite feature is the leaded stained glass windows.

The beer selection is all keg, with a lineup of well-known, familiar brands. I decided on a Level Head IPA; my pint was great, though the price point was a tad high. The food offering is traditional Roman-style pizza, with 15 options to choose from. A Margherita costs £11.

I arrived around 3:30pm on an overcast Thursday afternoon in October. The pub was quiet on arrival but soon started filling up with office workers from the surrounding area. The service was pleasant; the team member on duty was warm, welcoming, and courteous.

I enjoyed my visit here — my pint hit the spot. I loved the heritage of the building; the pizza receives good reviews, and those windows were great. Worth a look if you’re in the area

📅 16th October 2025

I went for lunch with some friends of mine. The owner accomodated us quickly, even if without reserved table. The pizza was the best I have had (potatos, tomato and sausages). The owner offere us a thinner bread/pizza with oregano as a started. The wait for food and drinks was minimum and spot on! I would teccomend the place for quality of food and incredibly friendly people. In few moments, we became friends of some regular customers. All the athmosphere is magnificent and you forget the stress of the city. The prices were incredibly low for the area. Unforgettable experience. It was my first time in this place, but I am planning to stop more often with my colleagues and friends.

Lovely pub! We popped in on a Saturday night before dinner and I only wish there’d been a few more people around! It deserves to have more costumers. The guy behind the bar was really friendly and shared some great beer recommendations.
Traditional British pub with fine beers and true Italian cuisine. We’ve tried a tasty Roman pizza (pinsa) with ham and tomatoes.
Reasonably priced food and drink, pizza here is genuinely one of the best ive had can tell its quality ingredients - £11 for a margarita in the city is very good value

I had the pleasure of photographing a beautiful wedding at Merchant Taylors’ Hall this year, and the entire experience was exceptional. The venue itself is truly stunning — full of history, warmth and atmosphere — it feels like stepping into a fairytale.

The staff were outstanding throughout the day. I especially want to highlight Donique, who looked after the couple and coordinated the timings seamlessly. The catering was also excellent, and the service was thoughtful and attentive from start to finish.

I can’t recommend Merchant Taylors’ Hall enough as a wedding venue — it’s a truly magical place to celebrate love, with a team who genuinely care about creating a perfect day.
Beautiful historic place in central London. Nearest station is Bank. Great place to host conferences like the one I attended'Livery Climate Conference'

As a wedding photographer, Merchant Taylors’ Hall is hands down one of my favourite venues to shoot at. It’s such a stunning and elegant place—every room is filled with character and charm, and there are beautiful backdrops everywhere you look. It’s honestly a dream location for capturing those timeless, romantic moments.

Guests are always wowed by the atmosphere too. There’s so much space to celebrate, mingle, and enjoy the day in style. And the team at Merchant Taylors’—especially Mohamed—is fantastic. They’re super friendly, professional, and always go above and beyond to make sure everything runs smoothly.

It’s definitely one of those venues I always look forward to going back to.

Best Regards
Doville Gail Photography

Merchant Taylors' Hall offers a unique blend of historic grandeur and modern amenities in the heart of London. Its stunning Great Hall, beautiful courtyard garden, and variety of elegant rooms make it a popular choice for events. Visitors often praise the impeccable service and delicious catering, making it a memorable experience.
Great food and great service. Such a beautiful building!!

We had an amazing dining experience here!

The food was incredibly authentic and reminded us of real home-style Chinese cooking.

Every dish was full of flavour and cooked perfectly.

The variety on the table was impressive—from fresh seafood to classic stir-fried dishes and savory braised meats. The lamb spine in a pot was beautifully cooked.

The dumplings and vegetables were also excellent, and everything tasted balanced and not overly greasy.
You can really tell the chefs know traditional Chinese flavors. The ingredients tasted fresh and the portions were generous, which made it perfect for sharing with family and friends.
If you’re looking for authentic Chinese cuisine, this place is definitely worth visiting. Highly recommended, and we will absolutely come back again!

Been a long time customer at this place and honestly never disappointed me. The food won’t blow you away but definitely hits the spot. It’s a northeastern Chinese restaurant so personally I would say it’s not exactly my flavor profile. But nonetheless, amazing stuff over here.

I no longer recommend this restaurant. I used to return for the tasty food and reasonable portions, and I accepted that service was minimal. Unfortunately, things have gone downhill. The service remains cold, but now the food is overpriced and the portions have noticeably shrunk. Rice is £3 per person, and even refills are no longer free. We ordered the spicy boiled beef, which cost £19.30. The same dish at a Sichuan restaurant near Moorgate is £15.80 (even with a 12.5% service charge, it’s still better value). Although there’s no service charge here, the food prices feel inflated to compensate. Vegetable dishes now come with half a plate. Overall, the quality just isn’t there anymore to compensate the bad service.

This place still pulls in a big crowd of Chinese students and locals, and portions remain huge. The spicy dishes can still deliver flavour when they’re on form, but my latest visit (Sunday, first customers of the day) was a real disappointment.The food:  Beef noodles and special Lo Mein were over-boiled and mushy, broths watery and oddly bland.
Lamb skewers (£2 each) and chicken wing (£2) were under-seasoned and forgettable.
It tasted nothing like previous visits either the chef has changed or standards have slipped badly.

The service:
The infamous “angry waitress” is unfortunately still there. My friend politely asked for two glasses of water and was met with a glare and an audible huff. Even her own colleagues seemed to keep their distance. The attitude was genuinely unpleasant and set a sour tone from the start. Large portions mean nothing when flavour and quality are missing. With far better options just a 5-minute walk away (Yeye’s, for one), there’s no reason to put up with sub-par cooking and hostile service.

Quite authentic Sichuan and Dongbei (north-eastern) Chinese foods. I’ve been here four or five times already.
My only complaint was that sometimes we had to wait to be seated quite long and unattended. But I think it’s fine unless you’re super sensitive to this.

Alright hear me now, I was influenced to go and try the £15 Friday smash burger deal at 1 Lombard street. I went with high hopes and my friend Olivia. This was a unique experience because this is the real life evidence of looks can be deceiving because the restaurant looks lovely inside, the food looks great but it all went very left very quickly.

We started of the meal having Oysters, now I’ve never tried oysters before so Olivia got them and I tried one and that’s when it all went sideways,  because I severely regret trying it them. They were watery, the texture was truly horrible and the lemon and Tabasco sauce did absolutely nothing for me. I can say it was the single worst thing I’ve eaten in my life. That was just the start to this chaotic culinary experience.

After quite a long wait the star of the show arrived the double party smashed burger with added burger for an extra £3 and a coke on the side for about £4.50. BUT did I get my coke ? No, I did not I thought maybe the waiter forgot so I reminded him and asked for some sauce to go with my chips he came back 5 minutes later with ketchup and what I hope was mayo but looked a lot like butter. The chips were good I will give them that, salty, crispy and fluffy can’t go wrong. The burger on the other hand wasn’t, it was purely texture and cheese because the patties didn’t taste of anything, the sauce didn’t add much because it was overpowered by the cheese, the pickles were lost in the burger and the bacon had no crisp and was chewy so I paid an extra £3 for weatherspoons quality bacon. Not only was all the moisture sucked out of my mouth  from the burger I didn’t have any water left to alleviate that as they would pour some in my glass and take the jug away with them and my coke, it  never arrived.

The coke wasn’t added to the bill which I don’t know how to feel about it but anyway if I was to give a recommendation after that experience I would say don’t bother, use your money else where and although it’s nice in there, lovely aesthetic but you could probably get better food and service elsewhere.
Our table enjoyed a lovely afternoon. Rodrigo was an excellent waiter, he looked after us very well. The rest of the team were great too. What a lovely find, we’ll definitely be back. Thank you!!

Upon entering I really liked the decor and how bright it was. We was seen straight away and then made our way to our table where drinks were flowing as we got the bottomless drinks for £20 each which was really nice.

We had Oysters for the starter and my partner wasn't the biggest fan as they are quite big. Tasty and was more for me lool.

For our mains, I decided to get the roast chicken and mrs got the beef which I wish I got after tasting it and was so good. The chicken was a lil dry but adding the gravy made it a lot better.

I would highly recommend if you want a nice date lunch or dinner.

Really good service and polite staff.

10/10

Brunch is very punctual, with doors opening bang on 12pm and finishing at 2pm. Service is a bit slow for such a strict two-hour slot, so the time doesn’t quite feel long enough.

However, we had a very lovely time. The atmosphere is enjoyable and the food is standard, nothing particularly stood out.

Service is friendly and professional.

we visited specifically for a roast. The staff were friendly and attentive throughout our meal.

The roast was delicious, but for a table of three we were given only a small shared portion of vegetables and cauliflower cheese, which was a bit disappointing. Individual servings would have made the experience feel more generous and balanced.

Aside from that, it was a lovely visit — stunning interior, warm service, and a truly tasty roast.

reviews.text: This was recommended to me through my native Spanish friend so knew it would be good. Amazing staff very attentive I really left smiling because they’re were just so friendly they allowed me to try out my broken Spanish with ease ha. The foood wow 😮 so good great price near the city and we could hardly walk from the amount of food we had please try the seafood paella and pork crackling massive highlights for us

We visited this restaurant for a quick dinner, but we were thoroughly disappointed. The food was poorly prepared, oily, and had an unusual mix of spices that didn’t align with the cultural expectations we had. To add to our dismay, the restaurant was dirty, with disgusting toilets. The overall atmosphere was noisy and unwelcoming. Despite the staff’s kindness and friendliness, we left everything on the table and left the restaurant.

Food 0/5
Cleanliness 1/5
Staff 4/5

Overpriced and not worth the heartburn you’ll get.

Not bad, I am hoping to return with company so I can try their paella. It's pricey but it's worth the taste. The portions are small, which I didn't realize until after the one item I wanted to have came. Staff seemed nice.
I tried the octopus (Pulpo al Gallega), which I had expected to come on a bed of sliced potatoes, instead they did mash. It was really tasty.

I started the dinner with Botata with garlic sauce it was really nice, then the calamari crunchy and Yummi, after that i eat my special main dish Bayella 😍❤️ i adore it, if it was without chicken would be better ❤️

We ended up at Barcelona Tapas Bar by accident after a change of plans - and we’re glad we did. The food was great, portions generous, and everything felt authentic. The sangria was especially good, and the staff were warm and welcoming throughout. The space has a relaxed, cosy feel that made for a really nice evening. Would definitely come back.
